name: Republic of Abkhazia
description: The Republic of Abkhazia emerged as a de facto independent state along the north-eastern coast of the Black Sea following its unilateral declaration of sovereignty in July 1992. The move triggered a fierce armed conflict with Georgia that concluded with the expulsion of Georgian administrative authority and large-scale ethnic displacement. Although it maintains functioning republican institutions and receives diplomatic recognition from a handful of foreign nations led by Russia, Georgia and the majority of international bodies continue to claim the territory as an integral autonomous republic. \n\n Status: De facto independent state with limited recognition; Capital and largest city: Sukhumi; Official languages: Abkhaz and Russian; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: People's Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 23 July 1992; Currency: Russian ruble and Abkhazian apsar

name: Republic of Angola
description: The Republic of Angola was formally reconstituted under a multi-party constitutional framework on 25 August 1992, transitioning away from its former Marxist-Leninist system. Despite the introduction of democratic elections, widespread hostilities with the UNITA rebel movement promptly resumed and persisted until the definitive ceasefire of 2002. Governed from the coastal metropolis of Luanda, the southwest African nation subsequently embarked on extensive post-war reconstruction driven by its expansive petroleum and diamond reserves. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Luanda; Official languages: Portuguese; Religion: Christianity; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Reorganised: 25 August 1992; Currency: Angolan kwanza

name: Czech Republic
description: The Czech Republic arose as a sovereign Central European nation on 1 January 1993 following the peaceful dissolution of Czechoslovakia. Embracing the historical territories of Bohemia and Moravia, the new republic consolidated parliamentary democratic institutions and rapidly transitioned towards a market-oriented economy centred on Prague. The state integrated firmly into Western international structures, securing membership in NATO in 1999 and subsequently joining the European Union in 2004. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Prague; Official languages: Czech; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 January 1993; Preceded by: Czech and Slovak Federative Republic; Currency: Czech koruna

name: Republic of Iraq
description: The Republic of Iraq experienced dramatic political transformations spanning the late Ba'athist era and the post-invasion reconstitution of the state. Governed by Saddam Hussein under crippling international sanctions following the Gulf War, the regime collapsed when a United States-led coalition invaded in March 2003. Sovereign authority was restored to an Iraqi interim administration on 28 June 2004, initiating a federal parliamentary republic that contended with prolonged insurgencies, sectarian conflict and reconstruction efforts from Baghdad. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Baghdad; Official languages: Arabic and Kurdish; Religion: Islam; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Legislature: Council of Representatives; Historical era: Contemporary; Currency: Iraqi dinar

name: Slovak Republic
description: The Slovak Republic came into being on 1 January 1993 as an independent Central European state upon the agreed division of Czechoslovakia. Anchored at its capital of Bratislava along the Danube, the country established its own democratic governance and gradually implemented structural economic reforms. Slovakia joined both NATO and the European Union in 2004, ultimately adopting the euro currency in 2009 while maintaining close diplomatic and economic ties with its neighbours. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Bratislava; Official languages: Slovak; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 January 1993; Preceded by: Czech and Slovak Federative Republic; Currency: Slovak koruna and Euro

name: Somali African Muki Organization
description: The Somali African Muki Organisation functioned as a socio-political and defensive organisation representing the marginalised Somali Bantu farming communities of southern Somalia during the civil war. Evolving from an agricultural advocacy association founded in the 1980s, the group mobilised to protect agrarian riverine settlements against predatory pastoralist warlords after the collapse of the central state. Despite lacking extensive military weaponry, the organisation gained international diplomatic recognition and took part in the Addis Ababa reconciliation conferences in 1993 before merging into broader transitional structures. \n\n Status: Faction and political movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Mobile council; Common languages: Somali and Maay; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 1993; Disestablished: 1 September 2000; Historical region: Southern Somalia

name: Somali Democratic Movement
description: The Somali Democratic Movement operated as an armed political faction primarily supported by the Rahanweyn agricultural clans across the inter-riverine Bay and Bakool regions of southern Somalia. Formed in 1989 to oppose the authoritarian government of Siad Barre, the movement sought to secure local autonomy and protect regional communities from encroaching clan militias. Throughout the 1990s, internal factional divides periodically fractured the organisation around Baidoa until many of its leaders helped inaugurate the Transitional National Government in 2000. \n\n Status: Rebel faction and political movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Baidoa; Common languages: Maay and Somali; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military council; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 1993; Disestablished: 1 September 2000

name: Somali National Front
description: The Somali National Front was established in the early 1990s as a politico-military organisation composed largely of Marehan clan members and loyalist remnants of the ousted Somali National Army. Operating primarily throughout the southwestern Gedo region, the front initially sought to restore deposed president Mohamed Siad Barre to power before shifting towards regional territorial defence. Under commanders such as Omar Haji Masallah, the group engaged rival warlords and Islamist militants until integrating into the nascent Transitional National Government in 2000. \n\n Status: Armed faction; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Garbaharey; Common languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military council; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 1993; Disestablished: 1 September 2000

name: Somali Patriotic Movement
description: The Somali Patriotic Movement was an influential armed faction drawing its primary support from the Ogaden clan across the southern Jubaland region. Founded by disaffected military officers in 1989, the movement participated in the coalition that ousted Siad Barre before fracturing into rival wings during the struggle for control over Kismayo. Operating without a formal administrative seat, the faction governed through local militia commanders across Lower Juba until broader diplomatic negotiations concluded with the formation of the Transitional National Government. \n\n Status: Rebel faction; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Kismayo; Common languages: Somali; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military faction; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 1993; Disestablished: 1 September 2000; Historical region: Jubaland

name: Somali Salvation Democratic Front
description: The Somali Salvation Democratic Front was an armed political organisation rooted among the Majeerteen clan of northeastern Somalia. Having spearheaded early resistance to the Siad Barre dictatorship throughout the late 1970s and 1980s, the front effectively secured stability across Mudug, Nugaal and Bari following the complete collapse of national authority. Under the leadership of Abdullahi Yusuf Ahmed, the front established stable local administration that culminated in the declaration of the autonomous State of Puntland in 1998. \n\n Status: Political and military organisation; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Garowe; Common languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military-civil council; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 1993; Disestablished: 1 September 2000

name: Kyrgyz Republic
description: The Kyrgyz Republic adopted its official constitutional designation on 5 May 1993, consolidating its sovereign identity following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. Located across the rugged mountainous terrain of the Tian Shan and Pamir ranges in Central Asia, the state maintained Bishkek as its political and economic capital. The republic navigated significant political changes, including popular revolutions and constitutional adjustments between parliamentary and presidential governance, while balancing diplomatic ties with neighbouring regional powers. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Bishkek; Official languages: Kyrgyz and Russian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Supreme Council; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 5 May 1993; Currency: Kyrgyzstani som

name: Talysh-Mughan Autonomous Republic
description: The Talysh-Mughan Autonomous Republic was a short-lived self-proclaimed autonomous entity declared in southeastern Azerbaijan on 21 June 1993 amidst national political instability. Headed by military officer Alikram Hummatov from the regional capital of Lankaran, the administration claimed jurisdiction over seven southern districts inhabited predominantly by ethnic Talysh. Lacking substantial political backing or popular consensus, the breakaway authority rapidly collapsed two months later when central government forces under Heydar Aliyev re-established official control in late August. \n\n Status: Unrecognised autonomous republic; Capital and largest city: Lankaran; Common languages: Talysh and Azerbaijani; Religion: Shia Islam; Government: Autonomous republic; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Alikram Hummatov; Established: 21 June 1993; Disestablished: 23 August 1993

name: Republic of Georgia
description: The Republic of Georgia operated during this brief period as an insurgent loyalist authority established by partisans of ousted president Zviad Gamsakhurdia in western Georgia. Centred largely throughout the historical province of Samegrelo, the Zviadist forces rejected the legitimacy of Eduard Shevardnadze's governing State Council in Tbilisi and seized several key transport hubs and towns. The rebellion was definitively crushed in November 1993 when government troops, reinforced by Russian military logistical assistance, overran the insurgent strongholds. \n\n Status: Insurgent government; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Zugdidi; Common languages: Georgian and Mingrelian; Religion: Georgian Orthodoxy; Government: Rival presidential government; Head of state: Zviad Gamsakhurdia; Established: 10 July 1993; Disestablished: 6 November 1993

name: Israeli Civil Administration (Military Occupation)
description: The Israeli Civil Administration in the Palestinian territories underwent profound structural realignment following the signing of the Oslo Accords on 13 September 1993. Subordinated to the Israeli Ministry of Defence and the military authorities, this administrative body retained direct civil and security jurisdiction across Area C, which encompasses over sixty per cent of the West Bank. Operating alongside expanding Israeli settlements, the administration oversees land zoning, planning permits, resource allocation and movement restrictions for the resident Palestinian population. \n\n Status: Military occupation administration; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Beit El; Official languages: Hebrew and Arabic; Government: Military administrative authority; Governing authority: Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories; Established: 13 September 1993; Historical era: Post-Oslo period; Currency: Israeli new shekel

name: State of Palestine
description: The State of Palestine gained widespread international diplomatic recognition and institutional footing following the signing of the Oslo Accords on 13 September 1993. Established initially under the Palestinian National Authority to govern designated enclaves across the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, its proclaimed capital remains East Jerusalem, while administrative operations are centred in Ramallah. The state exercises limited self-rule amidst continuing Israeli military control, territorial fragmentation and the internal political rift that emerged after 2007. \n\n Status: Partially recognised state under military occupation; Capital: Jerusalem (proclaimed); Administrative seat: Ramallah; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam and Christianity; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Palestinian Legislative Council; Established: 13 September 1993; Currency: Israeli new shekel and Jordanian dinar

name: Republic of Western Bosnia
description: The Republic of Western Bosnia, initially declared as an autonomous province on 27 September 1993, was an unrecognised secessionist entity situated in the northwestern corner of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Led by local politician and agribusiness director Fikret Abdić from the fortified town of Velika Kladuša, the enclave broke away from the central government in Sarajevo and collaborated with neighbouring Serb and Croat forces. The territory was twice overrun by the Bosnian Army before being permanently dismantled in August 1995. \n\n Status: Unrecognised secessionist state; Capital: Velika Kladuša; Common languages: Serbo-Croatian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: De facto presidential republic; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Fikret Abdić; Established: 27 September 1993; Disestablished: 7 August 1995; Currency: Deutsche Mark

name: Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was created on 18 March 1994 through the signing of the Washington Agreement, which brought an end to the armed conflict between Bosniak forces and the Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia. Governed from Sarajevo, the entity united the territories under Bosniak and Bosnian Croat control into a decentralised framework of autonomous cantons. This political arrangement formed a unified front against Serb forces during the remainder of the Bosnian War before being formalised as a constituent entity by the Dayton Agreement. \n\n Status: Constituent federal entity; Capital and largest city: Sarajevo; Official languages: Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Bosnian War; Established: 18 March 1994; Reorganised: 14 December 1995; Currency: Bosnian dinar and Croatian dinar

name: Republic of Palau
description: The Republic of Palau achieved full sovereign independence on 1 October 1994 following the conclusion of its United Nations trusteeship administered by the United States. Comprising hundreds of coral and volcanic islands across western Micronesia, the nation entered into a Compact of Free Association that guaranteed financial assistance and defence support from Washington. Operating initially from its historic commercial centre at Koror, the republic maintained a non-partisan presidential democracy and developed an economy centred upon eco-tourism and marine conservation. \n\n Status: Sovereign state in free association with the United States; Capital and largest city: Koror; Official languages: Palauan and English; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Palau National Congress; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 October 1994; Currency: United States dollar

name: Islamic Movement of Taliban
description: The Islamic Movement of Taliban originated in late 1994 around Kandahar as a Sunni fundamentalist armed faction composed of religious students and former mujahideen. Under the supreme leadership of Mullah Mohammad Omar, the movement swept across southern and western Afghanistan to suppress rival warlords before capturing Kabul in September 1996. Following its ouster by United States and coalition forces in 2001, the movement reorganised as an insurgent force in 2003, waging a protracted guerrilla war that eventually culminated in its return to power in August 2021. \n\n Status: Insurgent political and military movement; Capital and largest city: Kandahar; Official languages: Pashto and Dari; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: De facto theocratic militant movement; Head of state: Mullah Mohammad Omar; Historical era: Afghan Civil Wars; Established: 5 November 1994

name: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
description: The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia was formally inaugurated on 21 August 1995 upon the adoption of a constitution establishing an ethnic federal system. Headquartered in Addis Ababa, the landlocked Horn of Africa nation divided administrative authority among ethnolinguistic regional states while maintaining a strong federal parliamentary government. Despite facing significant regional conflicts and border disputes, the republic presided over rapid demographic and infrastructural growth while serving as the diplomatic seat of the African Union. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Addis Ababa; Official languages: Amharic, Oromo, Somali, Tigrinya and Afar; Religion: Christianity and Islam; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Legislature: Federal Parliamentary Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 21 August 1995; Currency: Ethiopian birr

name: Georgia
description: Georgia adopted its post-Soviet constitution on 24 August 1995, which formally renamed the state and established a stable republican framework following years of civil strife. Situated at the strategic juncture of Eastern Europe and Western Asia, the country maintained its political and cultural heart in Tbilisi. While striving for democratic consolidation, economic modernisation and closer integration with European institutions, Georgia has consistently asserted sovereignty over its breakaway territories of Abkhazia and South Ossetia. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Tbilisi; Official languages: Georgian; Religion: Georgian Orthodoxy; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 24 August 1995; Currency: Georgian lari

name: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia
description: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia existed as an autonomous Serb parallel entity along the Danube river following the collapse of the wider Republic of Serbian Krajina in mid-1995. Centred at Vukovar, the rump administration negotiated the Erdut Agreement in November 1995 to avert open conflict with the Croatian military. Under this diplomatic settlement, the region came under the temporary governance of the United Nations Transitional Administration, culminating in its full and peaceful reintegration into Croatia on 15 January 1998. \n\n Status: Parallel autonomous entity under United Nations supervision; Capital: Vukovar; Common languages: Serbian and Croatian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Unrecognised republic; Historical era: Yugoslav Wars; Established: 1 September 1995; Disestablished: 15 January 1998; Succeeded by: Croatia

name: State of Eritrea (Military Occupation)
description: The State of Eritrea established military occupation regimes across disputed frontier territories during distinct geopolitical confrontations in the Horn of Africa. The initial phase commenced in December 1995 when Eritrean armed forces seized the Hanish Islands in the Red Sea from Yemen, holding them until international arbitration awarded them back to Sana'a. Decades later, Eritrean troops occupied border sectors in northern Ethiopia during the Tigray conflict, deploying military contingents under the direct operational command of Asmara. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone; Capital: None (military occupation zone); Administrative seat: Asmara; Official languages: Tigrinya, Arabic and English; Government: Military occupation administration; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 17 December 1995; Currency: Eritrean nakfa

name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan
description: The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan was proclaimed on 27 September 1996 when Taliban forces captured Kabul, imposing an austere theocratic regime grounded in strict interpretations of Islamic law. Although commanding the vast majority of the country, the emirate gained formal diplomatic recognition from only three states before being overthrown by a United States-led coalition in December 2001. Two decades later, following the collapse of the internationally supported republic, the Taliban re-entered Kabul on 16 August 2021 to re-establish the emirate under supreme religious authority. \n\n Status: Theocratic emirate with limited recognition; Capital and largest city: Kabul; Official languages: Pashto and Dari; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary theocratic Islamic emirate; Head of state: Supreme Leader; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 27 September 1996; Currency: Afghan afghani

name: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire
description: The Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire was an armed coalition founded in October 1996 under the leadership of veteran dissident Laurent-Désiré Kabila. Backed by military coalitions from Rwanda, Uganda and Angola, the alliance operated initially from Goma in eastern Zaire during the First Congo War. Exploiting the terminal weakness of Mobutu Sese Seko's regime, Kabila's forces swept across the country within seven months, seizing Kinshasa in May 1997 and renaming the state the Democratic Republic of the Congo. \n\n Status: Insurgent coalition and transitional authority; Capital: Goma (operational headquarters); Official languages: French; Common languages: Swahili and Lingala; Government: Military revolutionary coalition; Head of state: Laurent-Désiré Kabila; Historical era: First Congo War; Established: 24 October 1996; Disestablished: 29 May 1997

name: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China
description: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China was established on 1 July 1997 following the handover of sovereignty from the United Kingdom. Governed under the constitutional framework of the Basic Law and the principle of one country, two systems, the territory preserved its capitalist economic structure, common law legal traditions and civil liberties. Situated on China's southern coast, Hong Kong expanded its role as a premier global financial hub while gradually experiencing deeper integration with mainland governance. \n\n Status: Special administrative region of China; Capital and largest city: Hong Kong; Official languages: Chinese and English; Government: Devolved executive-led system; Legislature: Legislative Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 July 1997; Preceded by: British Hong Kong; Currency: Hong Kong dollar

name: Independent State of Samoa
description: The Independent State of Samoa adopted its present title on 4 July 1997 after amending its constitution to remove the geographic prefix from Western Samoa. Occupying the two large Polynesian islands of Upolu and Savai'i alongside several smaller islets in the South Pacific, the nation is administered from its capital and main port of Apia. The country blends a Westminster parliamentary democracy with traditional fa'amatai chieftaincy customs, maintaining economic dependence on agriculture, tourism and overseas remittances. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Apia; Official languages: Samoan and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Legislative Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Reorganised: 4 July 1997; Currency: Samoan tālā

name: Democratic Republic of Mwali
description: The Democratic Republic of Mwali emerged as an unrecognised secessionist state on the island of Mohéli following its declaration of independence from the Comoros in 1997. Operating from the administrative centre of Fomboni, local leaders sought separation due to profound dissatisfaction with federal economic neglect and political domination by Grande Comore. Without gaining international recognition, the island retained autonomous self-rule for roughly two years until mediating talks yielded the Fomboni Accords, leading to its reintegration into a restructured federal union. \n\n Status: Unrecognised secessionist state; Capital and largest city: Fomboni; Common languages: Comorian, French and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: De facto presidential republic; Historical era: Comorian crisis; Established: 1998; Disestablished: 1999; Succeeded by: Union of the Comoros

name: State of Anjouan
description: The State of Anjouan was an unrecognised breakaway republic that declared its secession from the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros in August 1997. Centred at the historic port of Mutsamudu, the island administration was initially led by Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, who petitioned unsuccessfully for re-annexation by France before establishing independent governance. Although an amphibious Comorian military invasion was repulsed in late 1997, internal political fractures and international embargoes led to leadership changes and peace discussions culminating in the Antananarivo talks. \n\n Status: Unrecognised secessionist state; Capital and largest city: Mutsamudu; Common languages: Comorian, French and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: De facto republic; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim; Established: 1998; Disestablished: 1 August 1999; Currency: Comorian franc

name: New Caledonia
description: New Caledonia gained a distinct constitutional standing as a sui generis overseas collectivity of France on 20 July 1998 following the ratification of the Nouméa Accord. Located in the southwest Pacific Ocean, the archipelago is governed from its administrative seat at Nouméa on the main island of Grande Terre. The accord transferred substantial legislative powers to local institutions, recognised indigenous Kanak cultural identity and established a framework for successive self-determination referendums concerning the territory's political future. \n\n Status: Sui generis overseas collectivity of France; Capital and largest city: Nouméa; Official languages: French; Government: Devolved parliamentary dependency; Legislature: Congress of New Caledonia; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 20 July 1998; Currency: CFP franc

name: Rally for Congolese Democracy
description: The Rally for Congolese Democracy was established in August 1998 as a major armed rebel movement supported by Rwanda and Uganda to overthrow President Laurent-Désiré Kabila. Igniting the Second Congo War, the group rapidly occupied strategic urban centres across eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo while operating without a permanent civil capital. Ideological rivalries and geopolitical competition between its foreign patrons weakened the movement, leading to an acrimonious split in April 1999 that divided the rebellion into separate Rwandan- and Ugandan-backed factions. \n\n Status: Armed rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Goma; Official languages: French; Common languages: Swahili and Lingala; Government: Military-civilian rebel directory; Historical era: Second Congo War; Established: 2 August 1998; Disestablished: 1 April 1999

name: Movement for the Liberation of the Congo
description: The Movement for the Liberation of the Congo was founded in November 1998 by businessman Jean-Pierre Bemba to oppose the Kabila government during the Second Congo War. Backed militarily by Uganda, the faction established its administrative stronghold in the northern city of Gbadolite and exerted control across much of Équateur province. The movement administered territory and fielded a well-equipped fighting force until signing the Sun City peace agreement, which integrated its forces into the national transitional government in June 2003. \n\n Status: Rebel administration; Capital and largest city: Gbadolite; Official languages: French; Common languages: Lingala; Government: Rebel political-military administration; Head of state: Jean-Pierre Bemba; Historical era: Second Congo War; Established: 1 November 1998; Disestablished: 30 June 2003; Succeeded by: Transitional Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

name: Rally for Congolese Democracy–Goma
description: The Rally for Congolese Democracy–Goma was formed in April 1999 following a schism within the original RCD rebel coalition during the Second Congo War. Closely aligned with and militarily sustained by Rwanda, the faction established its headquarters at Goma and governed significant expanses of eastern Congo, including North and South Kivu. The movement maintained a parallel administrative apparatus and controlled mineral-rich trade corridors until formally dissolving its military structures to participate in the unified transitional government in June 2003. \n\n Status: Rebel administration; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Goma; Official languages: French; Common languages: Swahili and Kinyarwanda; Government: Rebel political-military administration; Historical era: Second Congo War; Established: 1 April 1999; Disestablished: 30 June 2003; Succeeded by: Transitional Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

name: Rally for Congolese Democracy–Kisangani
description: The Rally for Congolese Democracy–Kisangani was created on 1 April 1999 when founding chairman Ernest Wamba dia Wamba broke away from the main Goma-based leadership. Backed by the Ugandan military, the faction operated initially from Kisangani before being pushed into northeastern Orientale province following fierce clashes between Ugandan and Rwandan forces. The group subsequently relocated its operational base northward into Beni and Bunia, evolving into the RCD–Liberation Movement before joining nationwide negotiations that resolved the civil conflict. \n\n Status: Armed rebel faction; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Kisangani; Official languages: French; Common languages: Swahili and Lingala; Government: Rebel political council; Head of state: Ernest Wamba dia Wamba; Historical era: Second Congo War; Established: 1 April 1999; Disestablished: 2002

name: Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy
description: The Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy emerged in April 1999 as an armed insurgent coalition dedicated to the military overthrow of President Charles Taylor. Drawing support from Mandingo and Krahn veterans of earlier conflicts and operating with logistical backing from Guinea, the faction launched offensives from northwestern Lofa County. By mid-2003, the rebels had captured northern Liberia and laid siege to Monrovia, compelling Taylor to resign and go into exile before signing the Accra Comprehensive Peace Agreement in August 2003. \n\n Status: Insurgent faction; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Voinjama; Common languages: Liberian English and Mandingo; Government: Rebel coalition; Head of state: Sekou Conneh; Historical era: Second Liberian Civil War; Established: 21 April 1999; Disestablished: 18 August 2003; Succeeded by: National Transitional Government of Liberia

name: Union of the Comoros
description: The Union of the Comoros emerged as a reconstituted federal state in the wake of the 1999 Antananarivo negotiations to resolve protracted island separatism. Administered from Moroni on Grande Comore, the nation encompasses the three principal volcanic islands of Ngazidja, Ndzwani and Mwali in the Mozambique Channel. The constitutional framework established a rotating presidency among the islands to foster political stability, while the state continues to pursue economic development and claim sovereignty over the neighbouring French department of Mayotte. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Moroni; Official languages: Comorian, French and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Federal presidential republic; Legislature: Assembly of the Union; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 30 April 1999; Currency: Comorian franc

name: United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo
description: The United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo was instituted on 10 June 1999 pursuant to Security Council Resolution 1244 following the withdrawal of Yugoslav forces from the province. Headquartered in Pristina, the mission exercised sweeping executive, legislative and judicial authority to manage transitional governance, maintain public order and rebuild civil infrastructure. UNMIK progressively transferred administrative responsibilities to local provisional democratic institutions until the Kosovo Assembly issued its unilateral declaration of independence on 17 February 2008. \n\n Status: United Nations transitional administration; Capital and largest city: Pristina; Official languages: Albanian, Serbian and English; Government: International civil administration; Head of state: Special Representative of the Secretary-General; Historical era: Post-Kosovo War; Established: 10 June 1999; Disestablished: 17 February 2008; Currency: Deutsche Mark and Euro

name: Islamic International Peacekeeping Brigade
description: The Islamic International Peacekeeping Brigade was a radical Islamist paramilitary formation founded by Chechen and foreign fighters under the joint command of Shamil Basayev and Ibn al-Khattab. In early August 1999, the brigade crossed from Chechnya into the Botlikh district of neighbouring Dagestan to support local insurgent enclaves and challenge Russian sovereignty in the North Caucasus. Operating without a permanent municipal seat, the force held frontline mountain villages for mere days before formally declaring an Islamic state and engaging Russian federal forces in heavy combat. \n\n Status: Insurgent paramilitary brigade; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Botlikh sector; Common languages: Chechen, Russian and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Militant council; Commander: Shamil Basayev and Ibn al-Khattab; Historical era: War of Dagestan; Established: 9 August 1999; Disestablished: 10 August 1999

name: Islamic State of Dagestan
description: The Islamic State of Dagestan was a short-lived theocratic entity proclaimed on 10 August 1999 by insurgent leaders Shamil Basayev and the Islamic Shura of Dagestan. Centred within the heavily fortified Kadar zone around the village of Karamakhi, the rebels repudiated the Russian constitution and declared the implementation of Islamic jurisprudence. Russian federal forces and Dagestani loyalist militias launched a massive combined counter-offensive, systematically bombarding rebel positions and recapturing the mountain redoubts by mid-September 1999. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent theocracy; Capital: Karamakhi; Common languages: Dargwa, Avar, Chechen and Russian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic military council; Historical era: War of Dagestan; Established: 10 August 1999; Disestablished: 14 September 1999; Succeeded by: Russian Federation

name: United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor
description: The United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor was established on 25 October 1999 under Security Council Resolution 1272 following the withdrawal of Indonesian forces. Headquartered in Dili, the mission possessed direct sovereign executive and legislative authority over the territory, overseeing emergency reconstruction, civil administration and humanitarian relief. Led by Special Representative Sérgio Vieira de Mello, UNTAET guided the drafting of a constitution and democratic elections, concluding its mandate with the formal restoration of East Timorese independence on 20 May 2002. \n\n Status: United Nations transitional administration; Capital and largest city: Dili; Official languages: Portuguese and Tetun; Government: International civil administration; Head of state: Transitional Administrator; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 25 October 1999; Disestablished: 20 May 2002; Succeeded by: Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste; Currency: United States dollar

name: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
description: The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela was officially inaugurated on 20 December 1999 upon the promulgation of a new constitution spearheaded by President Hugo Chávez. Centred at its political and commercial capital of Caracas, the state initiated sweeping social programmes, constitutional restructuring and socialist economic transformations funded by its vast petroleum deposits. Over subsequent decades, the country experienced profound political polarisation, economic turbulence and institutional centralisation while maintaining its prominent role in Latin American regional geopolitics. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Caracas; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Christianity; Government: Federal presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 20 December 1999; Currency: Venezuelan bolívar

name: Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China
description: The Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China was established on 20 December 1999 upon the transfer of administrative sovereignty from Portugal. Situated on the western side of the Pearl River estuary opposite Hong Kong, the territory operates under the principle of one country, two systems, retaining its Portuguese civil law heritage and local autonomy. Macao emerged as a prominent global tourism and gaming metropolis, experiencing dramatic urban reclamation and economic growth while preserving its rich Sino-Portuguese cultural blend. \n\n Status: Special administrative region of China; Capital and largest city: Macao; Official languages: Chinese and Portuguese; Government: Devolved executive-led system; Legislature: Legislative Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 20 December 1999; Preceded by: Portuguese Macau; Currency: Macanese pataca

name: Islamic State of Afghanistan
description: The Islamic State of Afghanistan was reconstituted in Kabul on 22 December 2001 pursuant to the international Bonn Agreement following the military collapse of the first Taliban regime. Led by interim chairman Hamid Karzai, this transitional authority united anti-Taliban Northern Alliance factions and exiled political delegates under international and NATO security assistance. The interim administration oversaw initial post-war state reconstruction and convened an emergency loya jirga in mid-2002 to transition the government into a broader transitional authority. \n\n Status: Transitional interim government; Capital and largest city: Kabul; Official languages: Dari and Pashto; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Transitional interim administration; Head of state: Hamid Karzai; Historical era: War in Afghanistan; Established: 22 December 2001; Disestablished: 13 July 2002; Succeeded by: Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan; Currency: Afghan afghani

name: Islamic Emirate of Waziristan
description: The Islamic Emirate of Waziristan was an unrecognised militant proto-state established in 2002 across the mountainous tribal tracts of northwestern Pakistan along the Afghan border. Formed by local Pashtun tribal commanders alongside fleeing Taliban and al-Qaeda fighters, the administration enforced strict Sharia governance and challenged the authority of the Pakistani central government. The enclave served as a major logistical and training redoubt for regional insurgencies until Pakistani military offensives and tribal accords altered local control in September 2006. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent proto-state; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Wana; Common languages: Pashto and Urdu; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic tribal council; Historical era: War on terror; Established: 2002; Disestablished: 5 September 2006; Historical region: Waziristan

name: Rally for Congolese Democracy–Liberation Movement
description: The Rally for Congolese Democracy–Liberation Movement operated in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo as an offshoot of earlier rebel coalitions during the Second Congo War. Under the primary leadership of Mbusa Nyamwisi, the faction established administrative influence across the Beni and Butembo territories of North Kivu. Aligning progressively with the central government in Kinshasa against rival Rwandan-backed factions, the group governed without a formal capital until its armed units and leaders integrated into the national transitional government in June 2003. \n\n Status: Armed rebel faction; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Beni; Official languages: French; Common languages: Swahili and Nande; Government: Rebel political-military administration; Head of state: Mbusa Nyamwisi; Historical era: Second Congo War; Established: 2002; Disestablished: 30 June 2003; Succeeded by: Transitional Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

name: Rally for Congolese Democracy–National
description: The Rally for Congolese Democracy–National was a splinter faction formed under the leadership of Roger Lumbala during the later stages of the Second Congo War. Operating in the dense forest belts of northern Orientale province around Bafwasende and Isiro, the faction maintained tactical alliances with Jean-Pierre Bemba's MLC and received military supplies from Uganda. Lacking an official capital, the group maintained military control over local resource-rich sectors until formally acceding to the Sun City comprehensive peace accord in mid-2003. \n\n Status: Armed rebel faction; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Bafwasende; Official languages: French; Common languages: Lingala and Swahili; Government: Rebel military administration; Head of state: Roger Lumbala; Historical era: Second Congo War; Established: 2002; Disestablished: 30 June 2003; Succeeded by: Transitional Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

name: Kingdom of Bahrain
description: The Kingdom of Bahrain was officially proclaimed on 14 February 2002 when Emir Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa promulgated a revised constitution transforming the former emirate into a constitutional monarchy. Situated in the Persian Gulf between the Qatar peninsula and Saudi Arabia, the island nation is governed from Manama. The political transition re-established a bicameral parliament and instituted legal reforms, while the country expanded its position as a regional financial, refining and commercial centre linked to the Arabian mainland by the King Fahd Causeway. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Manama; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Islam; Government: Unitary constitutional monarchy; Head of state: King; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Reorganised: 14 February 2002; Currency: Bahraini dinar

name: Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
description: The Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste became the first newly sovereign nation of the twenty-first century on 20 May 2002 following the conclusion of United Nations transitional administration. Occupying the eastern half of Timor island alongside the coastal exclave of Oecusse and outlying islands, the republic is governed from its coastal capital of Dili. The young state established a semi-presidential democracy, rehabilitated essential infrastructure devastated during the 1999 crisis and developed its offshore petroleum resources to support national development. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Dili; Official languages: Portuguese and Tetun; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: National Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 20 May 2002; Preceded by: United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor; Currency: United States dollar and Timor-Leste centavo coins

name: Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan
description: The Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan was established in July 2002 by the emergency loya jirga to succeed the initial interim administration following the fall of the Taliban. Headed by President Hamid Karzai in Kabul, the transitional authority was tasked with reconciling regional factions, reforming the judiciary and disarming regional militias under the protection of international security forces. Its primary achievement was the drafting and promulgation of the democratic 2004 constitution, which paved the way for the formal establishment of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan. \n\n Status: Transitional sovereign government; Capital and largest city: Kabul; Official languages: Pashto and Dari; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Transitional presidential republic; Head of state: Hamid Karzai; Historical era: War in Afghanistan; Established: 13 July 2002; Disestablished: 26 January 2004; Succeeded by: Islamic Republic of Afghanistan; Currency: Afghan afghani

name: State Union of Serbia and Montenegro
description: The State Union of Serbia and Montenegro was established on 4 February 2003, formally reconstituting the former Federal Republic of Yugoslavia into a loose confederation. Governed from Belgrade, the union maintained joint foreign policy, defence and ministerial structures while granting both constituent republics separate economic policies, trade regulations and currencies. Designed to stabilise regional tensions under European Union mediation, the confederation functioned until June 2006, when Montenegro declared independence following a nationwide democratic referendum, leading Serbia to succeed the remaining union. \n\n Status: Confederated political union; Capital and largest city: Belgrade; Official languages: Serbian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Confederated semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Federal Assembly; Historical era: Post-Yugoslav transition; Established: 4 February 2003; Disestablished: 5 June 2006; Preceded by: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; Succeeded by: Republic of Serbia and Montenegro

name: Coalition of the Willing (Military Occupation)
description: The Coalition of the Willing functioned as the United States-led multinational combat coalition that launched the military invasion of Iraq on 21 March 2003. Operating under joint military command without a permanent civilian capital, the force rapidly advanced through southern Iraq to topple the Ba'athist government and secure Baghdad by early April. This brief transitional phase encompassed major combat operations and the collapse of Iraqi central authority, concluding when formal occupation duties were transferred to the newly formed Coalition Provisional Authority. \n\n Status: Military occupation and combat coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Coalition Forward Command; Government: Multinational military command; Historical era: Iraq War; Established: 21 March 2003; Disestablished: 15 April 2003; Succeeded by: Coalition Provisional Authority; Currency: United States dollar and Iraqi dinar

name: Territory of the Wallis and Futuna Islands
description: The Territory of the Wallis and Futuna Islands became an overseas collectivity of France on 28 March 2003 following French constitutional revisions regarding overseas territories. Situated in the South Pacific Ocean between Fiji and Samoa, the collectivity is administered from Mata-Utu on the island of Uvea. The political framework uniquely integrates French republican administrative law with customary governance, recognising three traditional Polynesian kingships alongside a territorial assembly and a French state administrator. \n\n Status: Overseas collectivity of France; Capital and largest city: Mata-Utu; Official languages: French; Common languages: Wallisian and Futunan; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Devolved parliamentary dependency; Legislature: Territorial Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Reorganised: 28 March 2003; Currency: CFP franc

name: Movement for Democracy in Liberia
description: The Movement for Democracy in Liberia emerged in early 2003 as an armed rebel movement operating primarily across the southeastern counties of Liberia. Backed by the government of neighbouring Ivory Coast and largely composed of ethnic Krahn fighters, the faction opened a decisive second front against President Charles Taylor's embattled security forces. Operating without a formal capital seat, the group quickly seized key coastal ports including Buchanan before joining peace negotiations that established the National Transitional Government in August 2003. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Buchanan; Common languages: Liberian English and Krahn; Government: Rebel military directory; Head of state: Thomas Nimely; Historical era: Second Liberian Civil War; Established: 1 April 2003; Disestablished: 18 August 2003; Succeeded by: National Transitional Government of Liberia

name: Coalition Provisional Authority
description: The Coalition Provisional Authority was created on 15 April 2003 as the transitional governing administration of Iraq following the overthrow of Saddam Hussein's regime. Operating from the heavily fortified Republican Palace complex in Baghdad's Green Zone, administrator Paul Bremer exercised supreme executive, legislative and financial authority under United Nations recognition. The authority enacted wide-ranging de-Ba'athification decrees and disbanded the Iraqi military before transferring sovereign governance to the Iraqi Interim Government on 28 June 2004. \n\n Status: Provisional occupation administration; Capital and largest city: Baghdad; Official languages: English and Arabic; Government: Transitional civil-military administration; Head of state: Administrator Paul Bremer; Historical era: Iraq War; Established: 15 April 2003; Disestablished: 28 June 2004; Preceded by: Ba'athist Iraq; Succeeded by: Republic of Iraq; Currency: United States dollar and Iraqi dinar

name: Islamic Republic of Afghanistan
description: The Islamic Republic of Afghanistan was proclaimed on 26 January 2004 following the ratification of a democratic constitution by the loya jirga. Administered from Kabul under presidents Hamid Karzai and Ashraf Ghani, the republic built representative institutions, expanded civil liberties and received extensive economic assistance from NATO allies. Despite major infrastructural and social developments, the state grappled with persistent administrative corruption and an intensifying Taliban insurgency, collapsing abruptly when coalition forces withdrew in August 2021. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital and largest city: Kabul; Official languages: Pashto and Dari; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential Islamic republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 26 January 2004; Disestablished: 16 August 2021; Succeeded by: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan; Currency: Afghan afghani

name: National Congress for the Defence of the People
description: The National Congress for the Defence of the People was an armed rebel movement founded in May 2004 by dissident general Laurent Nkunda in North Kivu. Supported by regional Rwandan networks, the faction proclaimed itself a defensive organisation protecting local Congolese Tutsi communities against Hutu militias. The group established de facto administrative control across swathes of the Rutshuru and Masisi territories before Nkunda was arrested in January 2009, leading the movement to integrate into the Congolese armed forces. \n\n Status: Armed rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Kitchanga; Official languages: French; Common languages: Swahili and Kinyarwanda; Government: Rebel political-military administration; Head of state: Laurent Nkunda; Historical era: Kivu conflict; Established: 25 May 2004; Disestablished: 22 January 2009

name: Union of Democratic Forces for Unity
description: The Union of Democratic Forces for Unity emerged in late November 2004 as an armed insurgent movement operating across the isolated Vakaga prefecture in northeastern Central African Republic. Based around the regional trading town of Birao and led by figures including Michel Djotodia, the group took up arms against President François Bozizé to contest political disenfranchisement and regional neglect. The rebels briefly held territory and key frontier garrisons during late 2004 before facing counter-offensives and subsequently signing peace accords. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Capital and largest city: Birao; Official languages: French; Common languages: Sango and Arabic; Government: Rebel military directory; Head of state: Michel Djotodia; Historical era: Central African Republic Bush War; Established: 23 November 2004; Disestablished: 23 December 2004

name: Montenegro
description: Montenegro declared its sovereign independence on 3 June 2006 following a closely contested national referendum that dissolved its state union with Serbia. Situated along the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea in the southern Balkans, the country is governed from Podgorica, with the historical settlement of Cetinje designated as the Old Royal Capital. Montenegro established a parliamentary democratic republic, pursued integration into Euro-Atlantic structures by joining NATO in 2017 and developed a vibrant economy centred on coastal tourism and service industries. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Podgorica; Official languages: Montenegrin; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament of Montenegro; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 3 June 2006; Preceded by: State Union of Serbia and Montenegro; Currency: Euro

name: Republic of Serbia
description: The Republic of Serbia was declared a fully independent state on 5 June 2006 following Montenegro's withdrawal from their shared political union. Located at the crossroads of the Pannonian Plain and the Balkans, the nation is administered from its historic capital of Belgrade along the Danube. The republic consolidated a parliamentary democracy, initiated economic modernisation programmes and pursued European Union candidate status while maintaining traditional diplomatic partnerships and contesting the international recognition of Kosovo. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Belgrade; Official languages: Serbian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 5 June 2006; Preceded by: State Union of Serbia and Montenegro; Currency: Serbian dinar

name: Islamic Courts Union
description: The Islamic Courts Union functioned as a confederation of local Sharia judicial bodies that established effective authority over Mogadishu and southern Somalia in August 2006. Arising from community efforts to suppress chronic banditry and warlord violence, the administration pacified the capital, reopened commercial ports and restored civic stability across large expanses of the Somali territory. However, its rapid expansion and radical rhetoric alarmed regional neighbours, prompting an Ethiopian military intervention in late 2006 that ousted the courts from Mogadishu by early 2007. \n\n Status: De facto Islamic administration; Capital and largest city: Mogadishu; Official languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic confederation of Sharia courts; Head of state: Sharif Sheikh Ahmed; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 1 August 2006; Disestablished: 1 February 2007; Currency: Somali shilling

name: State of Anjouan
description: The State of Anjouan re-emerged as a self-declared separatist entity in April 2007 under the autocratic rule of Colonel Mohamed Bacar. Rejecting federal Comorian authority, Bacar staged illegal local elections and established an independent island administration defended by loyal gendarmerie forces in Mutsamudu. The unrecognised secession provoked international sanctions and culminated on 25 March 2008 in Operation Democracy in Comoros, an amphibious assault by Comorian and African Union troops that toppled Bacar's regime and restored federal sovereignty. \n\n Status: Unrecognised secessionist administration; Capital and largest city: Mutsamudu; Common languages: Comorian, French and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military dictatorship; Head of state: Mohamed Bacar; Historical era: Comorian crisis; Established: 26 April 2007; Disestablished: 25 March 2008; Succeeded by: Union of the Comoros

name: Islamic Resistance Movement
description: The Islamic Resistance Movement, commonly known as Hamas, established exclusive de facto governance over the Gaza Strip in June 2007 following factional clashes with Fatah. Operating from its administrative seat in Gaza City, the organisation instituted a separate civilian administration, internal security apparatus and judicial system while maintaining its armed wing, the al-Qassam Brigades. Governed amidst strict border blockades imposed by Israel and Egypt, the movement engaged in repeated military confrontations with Israeli forces while retaining its political and social dominance across the enclave. \n\n Status: De facto governing authority; Capital and largest city: Gaza City; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: De facto one-party Islamist administration; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 15 June 2007; Currency: Israeli new shekel

name: Collectivity of Saint-Barthélemy
description: The Collectivity of Saint-Barthélemy became an autonomous overseas collectivity of France on 9 July 2007, having previously constituted an administrative commune within the department of Guadeloupe. Encompassing a small volcanic island in the northeastern Caribbean, the territory is administered from the historic port town of Gustavia. The collectivity exercises devolved powers over local taxation, land planning and tourism regulations, developing a prosperous luxury tourism economy while maintaining institutional representation in the French parliament. \n\n Status: Overseas collectivity of France; Capital and largest city: Gustavia; Official languages: French; Common languages: French and English; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Devolved parliamentary dependency; Legislature: Territorial Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 9 July 2007; Currency: Euro

name: Collectivity of Saint-Martin
description: The Collectivity of Saint-Martin was created on 9 July 2007 as a French overseas collectivity, detaching administratively from the overseas department of Guadeloupe. Comprising the northern portion of the shared Caribbean island of Saint Martin alongside several adjacent islets, the territory is governed from Marigot. The collectivity enjoys devolved legislative responsibilities concerning urban planning and transport, while maintaining an open land border with the Dutch constituent country of Sint Maarten and remaining an outermost region of the European Union. \n\n Status: Overseas collectivity of France; Capital and largest city: Marigot; Official languages: French; Common languages: Saint Martin English and French; Government: Devolved parliamentary dependency; Legislature: Territorial Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 9 July 2007; Currency: Euro

name: Republic of Kosovo
description: The Republic of Kosovo declared its independence from Serbia on 17 February 2008, concluding almost a decade of interim administration by the United Nations. Situated in the central Balkans, the landlocked state is governed from Pristina and features an overwhelmingly ethnic Albanian majority alongside Serb and other minority communities. Kosovo established a parliamentary constitutional republic and achieved widespread international recognition, although its sovereign status continues to be contested by Serbia and several other United Nations member states. \n\n Status: Partially recognised sovereign republic; Capital and largest city: Pristina; Official languages: Albanian and Serbian; Religion: Sunni Islam and Christianity; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Assembly of Kosovo; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 17 February 2008; Currency: Euro

name: Republic of the Union of Myanmar
description: The Republic of the Union of Myanmar adopted its current constitutional designation on 10 May 2008 following a nationwide referendum on a charter formulated by the military government. Situated in mainland Southeast Asia, the state relocated its administrative capital to the purpose-built interior city of Naypyidaw while Yangon remained its premier commercial hub. The constitution established a hybrid system reserved for military representation, initiating a decade of partial political and economic liberalisation before renewed military intervention sparked widespread civil conflict in 2021. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Naypyidaw; Largest city: Yangon; Official languages: Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Unitary presidential assembly-independent republic; Legislature: Assembly of the Union; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 May 2008; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal
description: The Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal was established on 28 May 2008 when its newly elected Constituent Assembly formally abolished the centuries-old Shah monarchy. Nestled in the Himalayas between China and India, the federal republic is administered from Kathmandu. The state completed a transition from civil war to a multi-party parliamentary democracy, adopting a comprehensive federal constitution in 2015 that divided the country into seven provinces and recognised its multi-ethnic, multi-lingual and secular heritage. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Kathmandu; Official languages: Nepali; Religion: Hinduism and Buddhism; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Legislature: Federal Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 28 May 2008; Preceded by: Kingdom of Nepal; Currency: Nepalese rupee

name: Harakat al-Shabaab al-Mujahideen
description: Harakat al-Shabaab al-Mujahideen emerged in late December 2008 as an independent Salafi-jihadist militant organisation following the retreat of Ethiopian occupation forces from central Somalia. Originating as a youth militia within the Islamic Courts Union, the group affiliated itself formally with al-Qaeda and established an insurgent proto-state across rural southern and central Somalia. Governed without a conventional administrative capital, al-Shabaab enforces strict Sharia codes, collects local taxes and wages asymmetric guerrilla warfare against the Somali Federal Government and African Union peacekeepers. \n\n Status: Insurgent militant proto-state; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Jilib; Common languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic militant organisation; Historical era: Somali Civil War; Established: 25 December 2008; Currency: Somali shilling

name: Plurinational State of Bolivia
description: The Plurinational State of Bolivia came into existence on 7 February 2009 upon the promulgation of a new constitution under President Evo Morales. The revised charter officially refounded the Andean-Amazonian nation to recognise the collective rights and cultural sovereignty of its thirty-six indigenous nations. Retaining Sucre as its constitutional judicial capital and La Paz as the executive and legislative seat of government, the state nationalised strategic resources, advanced indigenous representation and implemented extensive social development initiatives. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Sucre (constitutional); Administrative seat: La Paz (seat of government); Largest city: Santa Cruz de la Sierra; Official languages: Spanish, Quechua, Aymara and Guarani; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Plurinational Legislative Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 7 February 2009; Currency: Boliviano

name: Ansar Allah
description: Ansar Allah, widely referred to as the Houthi movement, originated as a Zaydi revivalist political and military movement in the mountainous Saada Governorate of northern Yemen. The organisation seized control of Saada during the 2011 Yemeni Revolution and subsequently swept southwards in late 2014 to capture the national capital of Sana'a. Governing vast swaths of northern Yemen through the Supreme Political Council, Ansar Allah has sustained an armed conflict against a Saudi-led coalition while entrenching an ideologically driven theocratic administration. \n\n Status: De facto governing authority; Capital and largest city: Sana'a; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Shia Islam (Zaydi); Government: De facto theocratic administration; Legislature: Supreme Political Council; Historical era: Yemeni Civil War; Established: 24 March 2011; Currency: Yemeni rial

name: Country of Aruba
description: The Country of Aruba reaffirmed its status as a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands following the wider constitutional restructuring of the Dutch Caribbean on 10 October 2010. Situated in the southern Caribbean Sea just north of the Venezuelan coast, the island is administered from its capital of Oranjestad. Aruba retains autonomous domestic governance with its own parliament, legal system and currency, while collaborating with the Dutch crown in foreign relations, common defence and judicial oversight. \n\n Status: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands; Capital and largest city: Oranjestad; Official languages: Papiamento and Dutch; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Devolved parliamentary representative democracy; Legislature: Parliament of Aruba; Historical era: Contemporary; Reorganised: 10 October 2010; Currency: Aruban florin

name: Country of Curaçao
description: The Country of Curaçao was established as an autonomous constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands on 10 October 2010 following the dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles. Located in the southern Caribbean off the coast of Venezuela, the island nation is governed from its historic port capital of Willemstad. Curaçao enjoys full autonomy in domestic legislation, finance and internal security through its parliamentary institutions, while sharing Dutch citizenship, foreign diplomacy and common defence within the wider realm. \n\n Status: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands; Capital and largest city: Willemstad; Official languages: Papiamento, Dutch and English; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Devolved parliamentary representative democracy; Legislature: Parliament of Curaçao; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 October 2010; Preceded by: Netherlands Antilles; Currency: Netherlands Antillean guilder

name: Public Body Bonaire
description: Public Body Bonaire was constituted on 10 October 2010 as a special municipality of the Netherlands upon the formal dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles. Situated in the Leeward Antilles off the Venezuelan coastline, the island conducts its local civil administration from the port of Kralendijk. Unlike the kingdom's autonomous constituent countries, Bonaire is integrated directly into the Dutch administrative and legal structure, with residents voting in Dutch parliamentary elections and utilising the United States dollar as legal tender. \n\n Status: Special municipality of the Netherlands; Administrative seat: Kralendijk; Official languages: Dutch and Papiamento; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Devolved special municipality; Legislature: Island Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 October 2010; Preceded by: Netherlands Antilles; Currency: United States dollar

name: Public Body Saba
description: Public Body Saba was established on 10 October 2010 as a special municipality integrated directly into the Netherlands following the dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles. Dominated by the dormant volcano Mount Scenery in the northern Leeward Islands, the territory is administered from its regional capital at The Bottom. With the smallest permanent population in the Americas, Saba maintains local governance through an elected island council while receiving public services, fiscal administration and infrastructural investment directly from the central Dutch government. \n\n Status: Special municipality of the Netherlands; Administrative seat: The Bottom; Official languages: Dutch and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Devolved special municipality; Legislature: Island Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 October 2010; Preceded by: Netherlands Antilles; Currency: United States dollar

name: Public Body Sint Eustatius
description: Public Body Sint Eustatius was created on 10 October 2010 as a special municipality of the Netherlands following the dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles federation. Situated in the northern Leeward Islands near Saint Kitts, the island's administrative affairs are centred in the historic harbour town of Oranjestad. The territory operates within the Dutch legal framework under a local island council and government commissioners, preserving its historical heritage as a colonial trading hub while relying economically upon regional oil storage, tourism and direct Dutch budgetary assistance. \n\n Status: Special municipality of the Netherlands; Administrative seat: Oranjestad; Official languages: Dutch and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Devolved special municipality; Legislature: Island Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 October 2010; Preceded by: Netherlands Antilles; Currency: United States dollar

name: Sint Maarten
description: Sint Maarten was established as an autonomous constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands on 10 October 2010 upon the dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles. Occupying the southern portion of the partitioned Caribbean island of Saint Martin, the territory is administered from its capital of Philipsburg. Sint Maarten exercises devolved authority over domestic taxation, police and infrastructure through its own parliament, while maintaining an open international border with the French collectivity to the north and sharing Dutch foreign relations and nationality. \n\n Status: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands; Capital and largest city: Philipsburg; Official languages: English and Dutch; Religion: Christianity; Government: Devolved parliamentary representative democracy; Legislature: Parliament of Sint Maarten; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 October 2010; Preceded by: Netherlands Antilles; Currency: Netherlands Antillean guilder

name: National Transitional Council of Libya
description: The National Transitional Council of Libya was formed in Benghazi in February 2011 as the political and military authority representing rebel forces during the First Libyan Civil War. Established to co-ordinate armed resistance against Muammar Gaddafi's regime, the council issued a constitutional declaration and obtained recognition from numerous foreign powers as the legitimate representative of Libya. Aided by NATO aerial interventions, council forces advanced across the country, captured Tripoli in August 2011 and declared the official liberation of Libya following Gaddafi's demise in October 2011. \n\n Status: Revolutionary transitional authority; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Benghazi; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Transitional revolutionary council; Head of state: Mustafa Abdul Jalil; Historical era: First Libyan Civil War; Established: 18 February 2011; Disestablished: 23 October 2011; Succeeded by: State of Libya

name: Republican Forces of Ivory Coast
description: The Republican Forces of Ivory Coast were constituted in late February 2011 by decree of internationally recognised president Alassane Ouattara during the second Ivorian civil conflict. Composed of northern New Forces rebels alongside defecting army units, the coalition launched a rapid nationwide offensive against forces loyal to incumbent Laurent Gbagbo. Moving without a fixed civil capital, the republican forces captured Yamoussoukro and besieged Abidjan, arresting Gbagbo in April 2011 before being reorganised into the restructured national armed forces. \n\n Status: Revolutionary military coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Bouaké; Official languages: French; Government: Military coalition; Commander: Guillaume Soro; Historical era: Second Ivorian Civil War; Established: 25 February 2011; Disestablished: 6 May 2011; Succeeded by: Armed Forces of the Republic of Ivory Coast

name: Department of Mayotte
description: The Department of Mayotte is an insular overseas department and single territorial collectivity of the French Republic located in the northern Mozambique Channel off the south-eastern coast of Africa. Comprising the main island of Grande-Terre alongside Petite-Terre and several surrounding islets, the archipelago formally transitioned from an overseas collectivity to a full French department on 31 March 2011 following a decisive local referendum. Administered from its prefecture at Mamoudzou, the territory forms an outermost region of the European Union where French civil institutions and European law operate alongside longstanding Shimaore and Kibushi cultural traditions. \n\n Status: Overseas department of France; Administrative seat: Mamoudzou; Official languages: French; Common languages: French, Shimaore and Kibushi; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Single territorial collectivity; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 31 March 2011; Currency: Euro

name: Syrian Interim Government
description: The Syrian Interim Government served as the alternative executive administration established by the National Coalition for Syrian Revolutionary and Opposition Forces during the Syrian civil war. Initially organised in exile in Istanbul before transferring its territorial headquarters to the northern city of Azaz, the authority exercised administrative oversight across rebel-held sectors and Turkish-administered border zones. Supported logistically by the Syrian National Army, the cabinet coordinated public services, civil documentation and local councils until relinquishing its functions to the newly established Syrian caretaker authorities following the collapse of the Baathist government. \n\n Status: Provisional government; Capital: Azaz; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary provisional republic; Historical era: Syrian civil war; Established: 18 March 2013; Disestablished: 30 January 2025; Preceded by: Syrian National Coalition; Succeeded by: Syrian caretaker government; Currency: Syrian pound and Turkish lira

name: Republic of South Sudan
description: The Republic of South Sudan is a landlocked sovereign state in East Africa bounded by Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Central African Republic. Traversing the White Nile basin and the vast seasonal wetlands of the Sudd, the nation gained formal sovereignty on 9 July 2011 following an overwhelming independence referendum that concluded decades of civil conflict against Khartoum. Governed from its national capital at Juba, the nascent republic has navigated fragile power-sharing arrangements, institutional reconstruction and deep socio-economic challenges under a transitional constitutional framework. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Juba; Official languages: English; Common languages: English, Juba Arabic and Dinka; Government: Federal presidential republic; Legislature: Transitional National Legislature; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 9 July 2011; Currency: South Sudanese pound

name: Republic of Kenya (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Kenya instituted a strategic military operational presence across southern Somalia from October 2011 following the launch of Operation Linda Nchi against the militant group al-Shabaab. Initially deploying ground forces across the border to secure its frontier against cross-border raids, Kenya coordinated its combat brigades through headquarters in Nairobi before later integrating its forces into the multinational African Union Mission in Somalia. The military administration supervised security zones throughout Lower Juba and established defensive garrisons around the strategic seaport of Kismayo to foster regional stabilisation and protect domestic transport corridors. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: Nairobi; Official languages: Swahili and English; Common languages: Somali, Swahili and English; Government: Military administrative authority; Historical era: Somali civil war; Established: 17 October 2011; Currency: Kenyan shilling

name: National Transitional Council of Libya
description: The National Transitional Council of Libya functioned as the provisional governing authority of the country following the armed overthrow and death of Muammar Gaddafi during the First Libyan Civil War. Having emerged from rebel councils in Benghazi, the executive transferred its administrative seat to Tripoli in the autumn of 2011 after securing formal diplomatic recognition from the United Nations and international partners. The council presided over post-conflict security, drafted interim constitutional declarations and enacted electoral legislation before peacefully handing sovereign authority to the newly elected General National Congress on 8 August 2012. \n\n Status: Transitional governing council; Capital: Tripoli; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Provisional transitional council; Historical era: Post-Gaddafi transition; Established: 27 February 2011; Disestablished: 8 August 2012; Preceded by: Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya; Succeeded by: General National Congress

name: Hungary
description: Hungary is a landlocked Central European nation occupying the fertile expanses of the Carpathian Basin along the Danube and Tisza river systems. On 1 January 2012, a newly enacted Fundamental Law came into effect, officially altering the state denomination from the Republic of Hungary to simply Hungary while reshaping national constitutional jurisprudence.
