Directed from its historic capital at Budapest, the parliamentary republic maintains an active regional presence in Central European affairs as a member of both the European Union and NATO while preserving its distinct Finno-Ugric linguistic and cultural heritage. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Budapest; Official languages: Hungarian; Religion: Christianity; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 January 2012; Currency: Forint

name: National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad
description: The National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad emerged in late 2011 as a predominantly Tuareg political and military organisation advocating for the self-determination of northern Mali. Leveraging desert combat experience gained by Tuareg fighters during the Libyan conflict, the movement launched an offensive across the Sahel in early 2012 and captured major urban centres including Gao, Kidal and Timbuktu. Operating without a permanent capital, the movement unilaterally declared the independent state of Azawad in April 2012 before suffering rapid territorial expulsion by better-armed Islamist factions and subsequently participating in regional peace negotiations. \n\n Status: Insurgent politico-military movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Tamasheq, Arabic and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Mali War; Established: 26 January 2012; Preceded by: Republic of Mali

name: Republic of South Sudan (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of South Sudan briefly established an armed military occupation over the contested Heglig border region during severe hostilities against the Republic of the Sudan in spring 2012. Motivated by unresolved boundary demarcations and control over lucrative petroleum installations, combat units of the Sudan People's Liberation Army captured the strategic oilfields in late March. Administered through operational field headquarters without a civil capital, the forward military enclave endured intense Sudanese air bombardments and sustained diplomatic pressure until southern troops completed an ordered withdrawal on 20 April 2012. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: None (operational field command); Official languages: English; Common languages: English and Dinka; Government: Military operational command; Historical era: Heglig Crisis; Established: 28 March 2012; Disestablished: 20 April 2012

name: Islamist Rebels
description: The Islamist Rebels constituted a militant coalition of Salafi-jihadist organisations, principally Ansar Dine alongside the Movement for Oneness and Jihad in West Africa and regional al-Qaeda affiliates, that seized control of northern Mali in mid-2012. Ousting secular Tuareg separatists following decisive clashes at Gao, the insurgent coalition imposed a strict interpretation of Islamic jurisprudence across major Saharan population centres including Timbuktu and Kidal. Governed through decentralised shura councils rather than a unified administrative capital, the factions maintained territorial control until French-led multilateral military intervention dispersed their frontline units into remote desert redoubts in early 2013. \n\n Status: Militant insurgent coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Arabic, Tamasheq and French; Religion: Sunni Islam (Salafism); Government: Consultative shura council; Historical era: Mali War; Established: 28 June 2012; Succeeded by: Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal-Muslimin

name: March 23 Movement
description: The March 23 Movement originated as an ethnic Tutsi rebel paramilitary group operating across the North Kivu province of the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Arising from a mutiny of former insurgents who accused the national government of violating a 2009 peace agreement, the movement seized substantial territory including the provincial capital of Goma in late 2012. Coordinated through field encampments rather than a formal state capital, the armed force suffered military suppression in 2013 before re-emerging in 2022 to mount renewed campaigns across the Rwandan and Ugandan borderlands. \n\n Status: Insurgent paramilitary movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Swahili, Kinyarwanda and French; Government: Military high command; Historical era: Kivu conflict; Established: 6 July 2012; Preceded by: Democratic Republic of the Congo

name: Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria
label: modern kurdish polities
description: The Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria arose during the Syrian civil war as a de facto self-governing polyethnic polity centred in the historically Kurdish regions of northern Syria. Founded upon principles of democratic confederalism, gender parity and local municipal autonomy, the administration established cantons spanning Jazira, Euphrates and surrounding districts. Headquartered administratively at Qamishli and defended by the Syrian Democratic Forces, the region provided civil governance and essential public utilities across north-eastern Syria while successfully countering extremist incursions and navigating complex diplomatic relations with Damascus, Ankara and coalition partners. \n\n Status: De facto autonomous region; Administrative seat: Qamishli; Largest city: Al-Hasakah; Official languages: Arabic, Kurdish and Syriac; Religion: Secular (predominantly Sunni Islam); Government: Democratic confederal direct democracy; Legislature: People's Democratic Council; Historical era: Syrian civil war; Established: 19 July 2012; Currency: Syrian pound

name: House of Representatives
description: The House of Representatives functioned as Libya's internationally recognised legislature and political authority in the aftermath of the 2014 national parliamentary elections. Confronted by armed Islamist takeovers and rival parliamentary assemblies in Tripoli during the outbreak of the Second Libyan Civil War, the deputies relocated their legislative seat to the eastern coastal city of Tobruk. Allied with General Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army, the eastern government exercised civil and military authority across Cyrenaica and parts of southern Libya until agreeing to support the unified Government of National Unity in March 2021. \n\n Status: Unicameral parliamentary government; Capital: Tobruk; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Parliamentary republic; Legislature: House of Representatives; Historical era: Second Libyan Civil War; Established: 8 August 2012; Disestablished: 10 March 2021; Succeeded by: Government of National Unity; Currency: Libyan dinar

name: Islamist Rebels
description: The Islamist Rebels encompassed a diverse array of Sunni armed factions and local coalitions that contested territory across northern and southern Syria during the Syrian civil war. Distinct from the transnational Islamic State, these formations included influential Salafist groups such as Ahrar al-Sham and Jaysh al-Islam seeking a state based upon Islamic jurisprudence. Operating through decentralised provincial shura councils rather than a single capital, these forces controlled vital rural pockets across Idlib and rural Damascus before being reorganised into integrated military operations commands in late 2024. \n\n Status: Insurgent armed coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam (Salafism); Government: Military shura councils; Historical era: Syrian civil war; Established: 11 October 2012; Disestablished: 27 November 2024; Succeeded by: Military Operations Command; Currency: Syrian pound

name: Séléka Coalition
description: The Séléka Coalition was an alliance of predominantly Muslim insurgent factions that coalesced in late 2012 to challenge the government of President François Bozizé in the Central African Republic. Originating in the economically neglected northern and north-eastern prefectures, the rebel advance swept southwards rapidly and captured the national capital of Bangui in March 2013, briefly installing Michel Djotodia as head of state. Lacking a centralised administrative structure and operating primarily through regional field commands, the fractious coalition later dissolved into competing regional splinter groups as sectarian clashes with rival Christian-animist militias engulfed the countryside. \n\n Status: Insurgent military alliance; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Sango and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Rebel military coalition; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 10 December 2012; Disestablished: 19 July 2024; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Islamic State
description: The Islamic State was an unrecognised militant quasi-state and transnational Salafi-jihadist organisation that gained extensive territorial control across north-eastern Syria and western Iraq during the 2010s. Proclaiming a worldwide caliphate in mid-2014 under Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, the group administered millions of subjects from its de facto capital at Raqqa, establishing rigid legal codes, tax collection systems and administrative departments. Following severe military defeats inflicted by international coalitions, Syrian Kurdish formations and Iraqi national armies, the organisation lost its final territorial bastions by 2019, reverting to clandestine insurgent cells across isolated desert pockets. \n\n Status: Unrecognised quasi-state; Capital: Raqqa (de facto); Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam (Salafi-jihadism); Government: Unitary totalitarian theocracy; Ruler title: Caliph; Historical era: War in Iraq and Syrian civil war; Established: 30 December 2012; Disestablished: 1 December 2024; Currency: Gold Dinar and Syrian pound

name: Democratic Front of the Central African People
description: The Democratic Front of the Central African People emerged as an armed opposition militia operating in the north-western borderlands of the Central African Republic. Initially founded by Abdoulaye Miskine, the faction took part in the Central African Bush War before briefly affiliating with the Séléka rebel alliance during the 2013 campaign against the central government. Stationed in remote rural strongholds near the Cameroonian frontier without a formal civil capital, the militia maintained territorial checkpoints between Kabo and Zoukombo, engaging in cross-border guerrilla operations and sporadic peace negotiations with national and international peacekeepers. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel militia; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: French and Sango; Government: Guerrilla military command; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 2 April 2013; Head of state: Abdoulaye Miskine; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Lord's Resistance Army
description: The Lord's Resistance Army persisted as a nomadic insurgent cult and guerrilla movement led by Joseph Kony across the dense wilderness dividing the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. Having been driven from its original base in northern Uganda through sustained regional military counter-insurgency, the movement sustained itself through abduction, looting and the illicit trafficking of ivory and minerals. Controlled from highly mobile jungle encampments rather than an established administrative seat, the weakened militant organisation retained sufficient operational capacity to evade international manhunts and terrorise remote rural settlements. \n\n Status: Insurgent militant movement; Administrative seat: None (mobile encampments); Common languages: Acholi and English; Religion: Syncretic Christian-animist cult; Government: Totalitarian military cult; Head of state: Joseph Kony; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 30 August 2013

name: Revolution and Justice
description: Revolution and Justice operated as a prominent non-state armed movement based in the north-western prefectures of the Central African Republic, primarily within Ouham and Ouham-Pendé. Established in the autumn of 2013 under the leadership of Armel Sayo, the group formed largely as a local self-defence initiative to protect civilian populations from both marauding Séléka units and predatory criminal bands. Lacking a civil administrative capital, the militia administered rural checkpoints and secured agricultural corridors until violent clashes with rival Fulani-dominated factions led to its military defeat and subsequent disbandment in early 2018. \n\n Status: Armed insurgent militia; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Sango and French; Religion: Christianity; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 1 October 2013; Disestablished: 30 January 2018; Head of state: Armel Sayo

name: Anti-balaka
description: The Anti-balaka developed as a decentralised network of Christian and animist vigilante self-defence militias in the Central African Republic following the rise to power of the Muslim-majority Séléka coalition. Mobilising rural youth, former soldiers and local village guards armed largely with machetes and hunting shotguns, the movement mounted sweeping counter-offensives across western and central prefectures, including fierce fighting in Bangui in late 2013. Without a unified civil capital or coherent political leadership, rival regional factions exercised local control over transit corridors and rural communities, frequently committing severe reprisal attacks against Muslim civilian enclaves. \n\n Status: Insurgent vigilante militia coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Sango and French; Religion: Christianity and Animism; Government: Decentralised militia councils; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 13 October 2013; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Popular Front for Recovery
description: The Popular Front for Recovery was a Chadian-led insurgent militia commanded by General Abdel Kader Baba-Laddé that operated across northern and central prefectures of the Central African Republic. During its brief active resurgence in early 2014 amid the collapse of state authority in Bangui, the faction established an operational garrison in the mining and market town of Bambari. Promoting the interests of nomadic Fulani pastoralists and disenfranchised border communities, the movement exercised local paramilitary dominance until intensifying clashes with rival ex-Séléka factions and French peacekeeping forces compelled its rapid tactical withdrawal. \n\n Status: Rebel insurgent militia; Administrative seat: Bambari; Common languages: Fula, Chadian Arabic and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 31 January 2014; Disestablished: 1 March 2014; Head of state: Abdel Kader Baba-Laddé

name: Army of the South-East
description: The Army of the South-East functioned as an early pro-Russian separatist paramilitary formation that seized administrative control across parts of Luhansk Oblast during the unrest in eastern Ukraine in April 2014. Occupying key regional security headquarters and government buildings in Luhansk without establishing a formal civil capital, the insurgent cadre was led by figures such as Valery Bolotov and received clandestine operational backing from the Russian Federation. The short-lived organisation spearheaded armed resistance against Ukrainian sovereign authority before formally reorganising its combat units to declare the self-proclaimed Luhansk People's Republic on 27 April 2014. \n\n Status: Pro-Russian insurgent paramilitary; Capital: None (operational command in Luhansk); Official languages: Russian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Revolutionary military council; Historical era: War in Donbas; Established: 7 April 2014; Disestablished: 27 April 2014; Succeeded by: Luhansk People's Republic

name: Donetsk People's Republic
description: The Donetsk People's Republic was an unrecognised pro-Russian breakaway quasi-state established across south-eastern Ukraine following armed seizures of regional government buildings in April 2014. Administered from the industrial city of Donetsk, the separatist republic functioned under extensive military, economic and administrative sponsorship from Moscow throughout the protracted War in Donbas. Heavily militarised and officially integrated into the Russian ruble zone, the puppet administration maintained fortified defensive lines against Ukrainian forces until the Russian Federation formally and unilaterally declared its annexation of the territory on 30 September 2022. \n\n Status: Puppet state of the Russian Federation; Administrative seat: Donetsk; Official languages: Russian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Legislature: People's Council; Historical era: War in Donbas; Established: 7 April 2014; Disestablished: 30 September 2022; Succeeded by: Russian Federation; Currency: Russian ruble

name: Luhansk People's Republic
description: The Luhansk People's Republic existed as an unrecognised pro-Russian separatist puppet state carved out of eastern Ukraine's Luhansk Oblast in the spring of 2014. Centred in the administrative capital of Luhansk, the breakaway regime operated through political leadership closely supervised by the Kremlin and heavily dependent on Russian military logistics, weaponry and financial subsidies. Controlling vital industrial centres along the Russian frontier during the Donbas war, the self-proclaimed authority held sham independence referendums and governed as a garrison state until being unilaterally absorbed into the Russian Federation in the autumn of 2022. \n\n Status: Puppet state of the Russian Federation; Administrative seat: Luhansk; Official languages: Russian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Legislature: People's Council; Historical era: War in Donbas; Established: 27 April 2014; Disestablished: 30 September 2022; Succeeded by: Russian Federation; Currency: Russian ruble

name: Kurdistan Region
label: modern kurdish polities
description: The Kurdistan Region functioned as an autonomous federal entity in northern Iraq that underwent substantial territorial and political expansion during the campaign against the Islamic State between 2014 and 2017. Governed from its regional capital at Erbil, the Kurdistan Regional Government deployed Peshmerga forces into security vacuums left by retreating Iraqi troops, securing contested districts including Kirkuk. Following years of effective self-rule and pivotal frontline action, the regional authorities organised a contentious independence referendum in September 2017, which precipitated a swift counter-offensive by Iraqi federal forces that re-established Baghdad's control over disputed oil-rich borderlands. \n\n Status: Semi-autonomous federal region; Capital: Erbil; Official languages: Kurdish and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Semi-autonomous parliamentary republic; Legislature: Kurdistan Region Parliament; Historical era: War in Iraq; Established: 5 June 2014; Currency: Iraqi dinar

name: Popular Front for the Rebirth of the Central African Republic
description: The Popular Front for the Rebirth of the Central African Republic was an armed insurgent movement formed in mid-2014 following the fragmentation of the broader Séléka coalition. Headquartered in the northern regional centre of N'Délé, the faction drew extensive support from Runga and Gula populations under the senior leadership of Noureddine Adam. Exercising de facto sovereign control over extensive stretches of the northern savannah, the movement collected municipal levies, controlled artisanal mining districts and defied transitional authorities in Bangui until formally proclaiming the separatist Republic of Logone in December 2015. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Administrative seat: N'Délé; Common languages: Runga, Arabic and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 10 June 2014; Disestablished: 14 December 2015; Succeeded by: Republic of Logone

name: Islamist Rebels
description: The Islamist Rebels in Lebanon formed an opportunistic incursion of Salafi-jihadist militants, predominantly associated with the al-Nusra Front and the Islamic State, that spilled across the rugged anti-Lebanon mountain frontier from Syria in August 2014. The insurgents launched a coordinated surprise assault against the north-eastern border town of Arsal, overrunning local police outposts and capturing dozens of Lebanese security personnel. Governed by tactical field emirs without a sovereign civil capital, the invading militant force briefly held town sectors before being repelled into mountain redoubts following a concerted counter-offensive by the Lebanese Armed Forces. \n\n Status: Insurgent paramilitary coalition; Administrative seat: None (frontline mountain bastions); Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam (Salafi-jihadism); Government: Military operational command; Historical era: Syrian civil war spillover; Established: 2 August 2014; Disestablished: 7 August 2014

name: National Salvation Government
description: The National Salvation Government emerged as a rival administrative authority in western Libya following the capture of Tripoli by the Libya Dawn militia coalition in August 2014. Reviving the mandate of the outgoing General National Congress and rejecting the newly elected House of Representatives based in Tobruk, the administration in Tripoli was led by Prime Minister Khalifa al-Ghawil. Supported by powerful armed brigades from Misrata and Islamist political factions, the government exercised de facto authority across Tripolitania until collapsing in April 2016 following the arrival of the United Nations-backed Government of National Accord. \n\n Status: Rival provisional government; Administrative seat: Tripoli; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Parliamentary provisional republic; Legislature: General National Congress; Historical era: Second Libyan Civil War; Established: 23 August 2014; Disestablished: 5 April 2016; Succeeded by: Government of National Accord; Currency: Libyan dinar

name: Union for Peace in the Central African Republic
description: The Union for Peace in the Central African Republic is a powerful politico-military rebel group formed in late 2014 as an offshoot of the dissolved Séléka coalition. Led by Ali Darassa and predominantly composed of ethnic Fulani pastoralists and combatants, the movement established its primary administrative and military base in the south-central mining town of Bria. The faction exercised expansive territorial control across the Ouaka, Haute-Kotto and Basse-Kotto prefectures, deriving substantial revenue through taxation of cattle-grazing corridors and illicit diamond extraction while periodically engaging in clashes with rival militias and governmental forces. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Administrative seat: Bria; Common languages: Fula, Sango and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 17 September 2014; Head of state: Ali Darassa; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Tuareg
label: tuareg polities
description: The Tuareg polity in south-western Libya functioned as an autonomous confederation of indigenous Amazigh tribal militias and local community councils during the turmoil of the Second Libyan Civil War. Operating throughout the hyper-arid Fezzan basin, including key border towns such as Ghat and Ubari, these pastoralist communities mobilised armed units to protect their cultural heartlands and secure vital trans-Saharan transit routes. Functioning through traditional clan elders and military commanders rather than a fixed civil capital, the confederation contested territorial and economic control against rival Toubou militias before formal local reconciliation agreements brought greater stability in 2019. \n\n Status: Autonomous tribal confederation; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Tamahaq and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional tribal council; Historical era: Second Libyan Civil War; Established: 5 November 2014; Disestablished: 1 February 2019; Historical region: Fezzan

name: Patriotic Rally for the Renewal of the Central African Republic
description: The Patriotic Rally for the Renewal of the Central African Republic was an insurgent movement founded in December 2014 by commanders who splintered from the northern ex-Séléka alliances. Rooted primarily among the Runga and Goula communities of the Haute-Kotto and Vakaga prefectures, the group maintained strongholds around Ouadda, Sam Ouandja and Tiringoulou. Operating without a sovereign capital, the armed faction governed regional trade routes, levied taxes on local commerce and engaged in territorial skirmishes with rival rebel factions until government offensives and international peacekeepers largely diminished its influence by mid-2024. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Runga, Arabic and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 1 December 2014; Disestablished: 5 June 2024; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula
description: Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula operated as a lethal Salafi-jihadist militant organisation that seized and governed significant territorial swathes across southern and eastern Yemen during the chaos of the Yemeni civil war. Reaching its geographical zenith in April 2015, the group captured the strategic coastal port of Mukalla in Hadhramaut, establishing a de facto proto-state that managed port revenues, municipal services and legal tribunals. Administered through frontline shura councils without an official national capital, the jihadist administration exploited local tribal grievances until an Emirati-backed military offensive liberated Mukalla and dispersed the fighters into mountainous interior hideouts in 2018. \n\n Status: Insurgent militant quasi-state; Capital: None (operational base in Mukalla); Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam (Salafi-jihadism); Government: Consultative shura council; Historical era: Yemeni civil war; Established: 16 April 2015; Disestablished: 29 April 2018; Currency: Yemeni rial

name: Islamists
description: The Islamists in Libya comprised an ideologically aligned confederation of autonomous Salafist militias and revolutionary shura councils that contested control of eastern urban centres during the Second Libyan Civil War. Operating primarily through umbrella organisations such as the Shura Council of Benghazi Revolutionaries and the Derna Mujahideen Shura Council, the fighters resisted the eastward expansion of Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army. Coordinated from fortified urban bastions rather than a singular state capital, these factions maintained entrenched defensive positions and enforced Islamic legal strictures until protracted urban warfare and sustained aerial bombardments broke their territorial strongholds. \n\n Status: Militant shura coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Consultative shura councils; Historical era: Second Libyan Civil War; Established: 25 July 2015; Disestablished: 19 July 2016; Currency: Libyan dinar

name: Central African Patriotic Movement
description: The Central African Patriotic Movement was an armed insurgent faction active across the north-western savannah of the Central African Republic between 2015 and 2021. Established under the leadership of Mahamat Al-Khatim following splits within the former Séléka rebellion, the movement drew support from Arab and pastoralist communities in the prefectures surrounding Kabo and Moyenne-Sido. Exercising de facto control over regional transit routes and livestock markets without maintaining a civil capital, the faction collected local tariffs until sustained counter-insurgency operations by national armed forces dismantled its territorial footprint in April 2021. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Chadian Arabic, Sango and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 1 August 2015; Disestablished: 15 April 2021; Head of state: Mahamat Al-Khatim

name: Islamic Republic of The Gambia
description: The Islamic Republic of The Gambia was the official designation assumed by the West African nation during the concluding year of President Yahya Jammeh's authoritarian presidency. Bordered almost entirely by Senegal along the lower Gambia River and administered from its historic capital at Banjul, the country was declared an Islamic republic in December 2015 to redefine national identity and deepen ties with the Muslim world. The change remained largely symbolic without overturning secular civil legal codes, and was promptly revoked in January 2017 following Jammeh's electoral defeat and exile. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Banjul; Official languages: English; Common languages: Mandinka, Fula and Wolof; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 13 December 2015; Disestablished: 29 January 2017; Succeeded by: Republic of The Gambia; Currency: Gambian dalasi

name: Republic of Logone
description: The Republic of Logone, also referred to as Dar El Kuti, is a self-proclaimed unrecognised separatist quasi-state established across northern districts of the Central African Republic. Proclaimed in December 2015 by Noureddine Adam and senior leaders of the Popular Front for the Rebirth of Central Africa, the administration designated Kaga-Bandoro as its capital. Operating parallel state structures complete with local gendarmeries, customs posts and rebel tribunals, the regime funded its operations through the exploitation of artisanal diamond and gold deposits while defying the sovereign authority of the central government in Bangui. \n\n Status: Unrecognised breakaway quasi-state; Capital: Kaga-Bandoro; Common languages: Sango, Arabic and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Provisional separatist administration; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 14 December 2015; Head of state: Noureddine Adam; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Government of National Accord
description: The Government of National Accord functioned as an interim sovereign administration created under the United Nations-brokered Libyan Political Agreement to heal national divisions during the Second Libyan Civil War. Led by Prime Minister Fayez al-Sarraj, the Presidential Council installed itself in Tripoli in March 2016, securing broad international recognition as Libya's executive authority despite continued resistance from the rival parliament in Tobruk. The administration maintained public institutions, repelled a major eastern military assault on the capital and participated in constitutional dialogues until handing over power to the unified Government of National Unity in March 2021. \n\n Status: Provisional government; Capital: Tripoli; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Transitional presidential republic; Historical era: Second Libyan Civil War; Established: 25 March 2016; Disestablished: 10 March 2021; Preceded by: National Salvation Government; Succeeded by: Government of National Unity; Currency: Libyan dinar

name: Republic of Azerbaijan (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Azerbaijan instituted an expansive military occupation across reclaimed regions of the South Caucasus following its tactical advances during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War in late 2020. Administered directly by armed forces operational commands without a permanent civilian capital, the occupied areas comprised surrounding security belts and key urban settlements, including Jabrayil, Hadrut and the historic fortress city of Shusha. Under heavy military governance and engineering supervision, Azerbaijani authorities conducted sweeping de-mining campaigns, constructed fortified logistic infrastructure and established security perimeters that paved the way for the eventual full reintegration of the entire enclave into sovereign Azerbaijani administration. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: None (military operational control); Official languages: Azerbaijani; Common languages: Azerbaijani and Russian; Government: Military administrative command; Historical era: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War; Established: 9 October 2020; Disestablished: 2024; Currency: Azerbaijani manat

name: Southern Transitional Council
description: The Southern Transitional Council is a secessionist political and paramilitary organisation advocating for the restoration of an independent South Yemeni state along the borders of the former South Yemen. Established under the leadership of Aidarus al-Zubaidi with crucial logistical backing from the United Arab Emirates, the council consolidated de facto control over the port city of Aden and surrounding southern governorates. Balancing military resistance against northern Houthi forces with administrative governance, the council secured significant regional authority before formally joining Yemen's power-sharing Presidential Leadership Council in April 2022. \n\n Status: Autonomous separatist political body; Capital: Aden; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Transitional presidium; Historical era: Yemeni civil war; Established: 25 April 2016; Head of state: Aidarus al-Zubaidi; Currency: Yemeni rial

name: Return, Reclamation, Rehabilitation
description: Return, Reclamation, Rehabilitation, widely known as 3R, is an armed insurgent movement active across the north-western prefectures of the Central African Republic. Founded under the leadership of Sidiki Abass with the declared mission of shielding Fulani herders from hostile Anti-balaka militias, the group established strongholds across Ouham-Pendé and Nana-Mambéré. Operating through mobile military bases rather than a formal civil capital, the faction financed its operations by taxing transhumance corridors and livestock trade, continuing to launch rural guerrilla strikes against state forces and international peacekeepers after Abass was killed in 2021. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Fula, Sango and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 27 September 2016; Preceded by: Central African Republic; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Republic of Artsakh
description: The Republic of Artsakh was an unrecognised breakaway republic in the South Caucasus, adopting this constitutional title in February 2017 as the formal successor to the Nagorno-Karabakh Republic. Centred at its administrative capital of Stepanakert, the self-governing entity maintained intimate political, economic and defensive ties with neighbouring Armenia while administering a predominantly ethnic Armenian population. Following heavy territorial losses in the 2020 conflict, the enclave suffered prolonged isolation before an Azerbaijani offensive in September 2023 dismantled its institutions, culminating in the formal dissolution of the republic and the flight of its inhabitants. \n\n Status: Unrecognised breakaway state; Capital and largest city: Stepanakert; Official languages: Armenian and Russian; Religion: Armenian Apostolic Christianity; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 21 February 2017; Disestablished: 2024; Succeeded by: Republic of Azerbaijan; Currency: Armenian dram

name: Federal Republic of Ambazonia
description: The Federal Republic of Ambazonia is a self-declared unrecognised breakaway state proclaimed by Anglophone separatists across the Northwest and Southwest regions of Cameroon. Formally declared on 1 October 2017 following escalating civil unrest over the perceived political, legal and cultural marginalisation of English-speaking citizens by the Francophone-dominated central government, the movement designated Buea as its historic capital. Operating primarily through competing coalitions in exile and local armed militias known as the Ambazonia Defence Forces, the separatists have engaged in protracted guerrilla warfare against Cameroonian security forces while exercising irregular control over rural hinterlands. \n\n Status: Unrecognised breakaway state; Capital: Buea; Largest city: Bamenda; Official languages: English; Common languages: English, Cameroonian Pidgin and indigenous languages; Religion: Christianity; Government: Provisional federal republic; Historical era: Anglophone Crisis; Established: 1 October 2017; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Kingdom of Eswatini
description: The Kingdom of Eswatini is a landlocked sovereign monarchy located in Southern Africa, sharing terrestrial borders with South Africa and Mozambique. On 19 April 2018, King Mswati III decreed the change of the country's official name from the Kingdom of Swaziland to Eswatini, meaning land of the Swazis, to mark the fiftieth anniversary of national independence and cast off colonial nomenclature. Governed under an absolute diarchic monarchy with its administrative centre in Mbabane and royal legislature in Lobamba, the state preserves traditional Tinkhundla governance alongside hereditary royal authority over its predominantly Swazi population. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Mbabane (executive) and Lobamba (legislative); Official languages: Swazi and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Unitary absolute diarchy; Head of state: King Mswati III; Legislature: Parliament of Eswatini; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 19 April 2018; Currency: Swazi lilangeni and South African rand

name: United Arab Emirates (Military Occupation)
description: The United Arab Emirates initiated a temporary military occupation over the strategic Yemeni archipelago of Socotra in the Indian Ocean in late April 2018. Deploying armoured vehicles, transport aircraft and military personnel to the island's primary airport and seaports without prior coordination with the internationally recognised Yemeni government, Emirati forces established forward operational control over critical transit infrastructure. Controlled from military command elements without establishing a civilian capital, this brief occupation triggered sharp diplomatic confrontations with Yemeni authorities until Saudi-brokered negotiations facilitated an administrative compromise and the withdrawal of Emirati forces two weeks later. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: None (military operational command); Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Arabic and Soqotri; Government: Military administrative command; Historical era: Yemeni civil war; Established: 30 April 2018; Disestablished: 14 May 2018; Preceded by: Republic of Yemen; Succeeded by: Republic of Yemen

name: Republic of North Macedonia
description: The Republic of North Macedonia is a landlocked sovereign republic situated in the Balkan Peninsula of South-Eastern Europe, bordered by Serbia, Kosovo, Bulgaria, Greece and Albania. On 12 February 2019, the state officially adopted its present name following the implementation of the historic Prespa Agreement, which successfully resolved a decades-long diplomatic dispute with Greece regarding the usage of the name Macedonia. Directed from its historic capital at Skopje, the nation functions as a parliamentary democracy comprising a Slavic Macedonian majority and a substantial Albanian minority, having subsequently achieved full accession to NATO in 2020. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Skopje; Official languages: Macedonian and Albanian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy and Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Assembly of North Macedonia; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 12 February 2019; Preceded by: Republic of Macedonia; Currency: Macedonian denar

name: Movement of Central African Liberators for Justice
description: The Movement of Central African Liberators for Justice was an ethnic armed organisation that operated throughout the north-eastern prefecture of Vakaga in the Central African Republic. Splintering originally from the Union of Democratic Forces for Unity and drawing its primary support from the indigenous Kara population under the command of Abakor Sabone, the group emerged to counter Runga dominance in the region. Lacking a formal civil capital, the faction conducted operations from rural strongholds near Birao, engaging in violent inter-ethnic confrontations over regional market routes until state forces and allied security personnel gradually pacified the province in late 2022. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Kara, Arabic and French; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military command council; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 2 September 2019; Disestablished: 4 December 2022; Head of state: Abakor Sabone

name: Tigray People's Liberation Front
description: The Tigray People's Liberation Front served as the governing authority and armed insurgent force of the Tigray Region during the Tigray War against Ethiopian federal forces and allied Eritrean troops. Headquartered in the regional capital of Mekelle, the leadership mobilised the Tigray Defence Forces after tensions with Addis Ababa escalated into full-scale conflict in November 2020. Despite suffering initial territorial losses, the organisation launched a massive counter-offensive in mid-2021 to reclaim its core territories, maintaining de facto resistance until signing a formal peace agreement in South Africa in late 2022. \n\n Status: De facto regional government; Capital: Mekelle; Official languages: Tigrinya; Common languages: Tigrinya and Amharic; Religion: Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity; Government: Left-wing regional administration; Historical era: Tigray War; Established: 4 November 2020; Disestablished: 29 December 2022; Succeeded by: Tigray Interim Regional Administration; Currency: Ethiopian birr

name: Arakan Army
description: The Arakan Army operated as a formidable ethnic armed organisation representing the Buddhist Rakhine people in western Myanmar during the escalating post-coup civil war. Functioning as the armed wing of the United League of Arakan under Major General Twan Mrat Naing, the movement established administrative headquarters in the historic royal capital of Mrauk-U. Taking advantage of the nationwide breakdown of junta control after February 2021, the army developed comprehensive parallel state structures across northern Rakhine, administering civil courts, public taxation and local healthcare, until formally rebranding its military and political apparatus as the Arakha Army in April 2024. \n\n Status: Autonomous ethnic administration; Capital: Mrauk-U; Official languages: Rakhine and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Military administrative council; Ruler title: Commander-in-Chief; First ruler: Twan Mrat Naing; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Disestablished: 10 April 2024; Succeeded by: Arakha Army; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Kachin Independence Army
description: The Kachin Independence Army serves as the seasoned military wing of the Kachin Independence Organisation, defending the autonomy of the predominantly Christian Kachin people in northern Myanmar along the Chinese border. Headquartered in the frontier redoubt of Laiza, the army renewed intense armed resistance against the Myanmar military following the February 2021 coup, providing crucial armaments, refuge and tactical training to newly formed pro-democracy resistance militias. The organisation maintains sophisticated bureaucratic ministries, collects revenue from local jade and rare-earth extraction, and has systematically expanded its liberated territory across Kachin State and northern Shan State through coordinated multi-brigade offensives. \n\n Status: De facto autonomous ethnic state; Capital: Laiza; Official languages: Kachin and Burmese; Religion: Christianity; Government: Ethnic revolutionary administration; Legislature: Kachin Independence Council; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Currency: Myanmar kyat and Chinese yuan

name: Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army
description: The Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army is an armed ethnic resistance organisation representing the Han Chinese Kokang population in the mountainous borderlands of northern Shan State. Operating under the leadership of Peng Daxun, the group joined the potent Three Brotherhood Alliance and intensified its long-standing campaign against the military junta following the 2021 coup. In late 2023, the army spearheaded Operation 1027, achieving a stunning operational victory by recapturing its historical stronghold and capital of Laukkai while eliminating notorious cross-border telecom scam compounds and re-establishing autonomous Kokang civil and economic governance along the international frontier. \n\n Status: De facto autonomous ethnic administration; Capital: Laukkai; Official languages: Kokang Chinese and Burmese; Religion: Chinese folk religion and Buddhism; Government: Special administrative region; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Currency: Chinese yuan and Myanmar kyat

name: Pa-O National Army
description: The Pa-O National Army is an ethnic paramilitary force acting as the armed wing of the Pa-O National Organisation within the mountainous expanse of southern Shan State in Myanmar. Established initially in the mid-twentieth century and restructured following historic ceasefire agreements, the army oversees security throughout the officially designated Pa-O Self-Administered Zone from its primary administrative base at Hopong. In the wake of the 2021 coup, the leadership aligned closely with the central military junta, engaging in forced recruitment, defensive garrisoning and joint operational sweeps to suppress anti-junta resistance groups attempting to infiltrate the Shan highlands. \n\n Status: Self-administered ethnic zone militia; Administrative seat: Hopong; Common languages: Pa-O and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Semi-autonomous militia council; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Historical region: Shan State; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: People's Defence Force
description: The People's Defence Force serves as the nationwide armed wing of the National Unity Government of Myanmar, created in May 2021 to oppose the military junta that seized power in a coup d'état. Formed largely by pro-democracy youths, striking civil servants and defectors, the organisation coordinates hundreds of local battalions across rural and urban theatres in close operational partnership with established ethnic armed organisations. Functioning without a centralised physical capital, the resistance force conducts guerrilla ambushes, drone strikes and regional administrative protection, growing into an expansive insurgent army that contests junta control across central Myanmar. \n\n Status: Revolutionary national defence force; Capital: None (decentralised nationwide network); Official languages: Burmese; Common languages: Burmese and indigenous languages; Government: Armed wing of the National Unity Government; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Preceded by: Republic of the Union of Myanmar; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Ta'ang National Liberation Army
description: The Ta'ang National Liberation Army is the armed wing of the Palaung State Liberation Front, representing the Ta'ang ethnic minority across the highlands of northern Shan State in Myanmar. Operating from its mountain stronghold and historical capital of Namhsan, the movement expanded its military capabilities following the February 2021 coup by forging strategic alliances with the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army and Arakan Army. Through the coordinated offensive of Operation 1027 in late 2023, the army liberated numerous strategic towns, seized vital trade arteries along the Chinese border and instituted self-administered local governance councils across Ta'ang lands. \n\n Status: Autonomous ethnic administration; Capital: Namhsan; Common languages: Ta'ang and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Palaung State Liberation Front administration; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Historical region: Shan State; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: United Wa State Army
description: The United Wa State Army is the heavily armed military branch of the United Wa State Party, governing the unrecognised de facto autonomous Wa State along Myanmar's north-eastern border with China. Headquartered in the thriving border city of Pangkham, the army commands an estimated thirty thousand well-equipped troops armed with sophisticated modern weaponry supplied via cross-border regional channels. Maintaining strict internal security, comprehensive civil services and an economy rooted in agriculture, mining and manufacturing, the Wa administration preserved de facto independence throughout the post-2021 civil war while leveraging its diplomatic influence over other northern resistance organisations. \n\n Status: De facto autonomous state; Capital: Pangkham; Official languages: Wa and Mandarin Chinese; Common languages: Wa, Chinese and Burmese; Government: Single-party authoritarian state; Head of state: Bao Youxiang; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2021; Currency: Chinese yuan

name: State of Libya
description: The State of Libya entered a fragile period of political reunification in March 2021 following the endorsement of the Government of National Unity through the United Nations-led Libyan Political Dialogue Forum. Headquartered in the capital city of Tripoli under Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh, the interim executive was established to integrate competing civil institutions and prepare for nationwide democratic elections. Despite initial progress in unifying state finances and military ceasefires across Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and the Fezzan, political instability re-emerged as the eastern House of Representatives later rescinded its confidence, maintaining a fractured administrative landscape. \n\n Status: Sovereign state under provisional government; Capital and largest city: Tripoli; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary republic under a provisional government; Legislature: High Council of State and House of Representatives; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 10 March 2021; Preceded by: Government of National Accord; Currency: Libyan dinar

name: Karen National Liberation Army
description: The Karen National Liberation Army serves as the military branch of the Karen National Union, fighting for the self-determination of the Karen people in south-eastern Myanmar along the border with Thailand. Established over seven decades ago, the army dramatically intensified its defensive operations after the February 2021 military coup, sheltering thousands of dissidents and coordinating anti-junta resistance battalions. Centred administratively at the model township of Lay Kay Kaw, the force withstood heavy artillery bombardments and airstrikes by the junta before mounting major counter-offensives that captured numerous military garrisons and vital frontier trade crossings. \n\n Status: Ethnic resistance army; Administrative seat: Lay Kay Kaw; Common languages: Karen, Burmese and English; Religion: Christianity, Buddhism and Animism; Government: Military command of the Karen National Union; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 27 March 2021; Historical region: Kayin State; Currency: Myanmar kyat and Thai baht

name: Oromo Liberation Army
description: The Oromo Liberation Army functioned as an armed ethnic insurgent movement contesting federal authority across the expansive Oromia Region of central and western Ethiopia during the peak of the Tigray War. Splintering from the historic Oromo Liberation Front following disagreements surrounding disarmament, the guerrilla army established a formal military alliance with the Tigray People's Liberation Front in late 2021. Operating without a fixed territorial capital, the insurgent brigades captured key towns along the strategic highway leading towards Addis Ababa before federal counter-offensives and armed drone deployments forced the fighters to retreat into their forested rural sanctuaries. \n\n Status: Insurgent armed movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Official languages: Oromo; Common languages: Oromo and Amharic; Government: Revolutionary military command; Historical era: Tigray War; Established: 26 October 2021; Disestablished: 20 December 2021; Currency: Ethiopian birr

name: Chin Forces
description: The Chin Forces comprised a broad coalition of ethnic Chin insurgent groups and local township civil defence organisations that mobilised across western Myanmar following the 2021 military coup. Uniting veteran combatants from the Chin National Front with newly established township People's Defence Forces, this collective alliance operated without a singular civil capital, relying instead on decentralised field headquarters in the rugged Chin Hills. Through coordinated guerrilla actions and indigenous knowledge of mountainous terrain, the allied fighters captured government outposts and administered autonomous mountain communities before formalising their unified political structure through the Chinland Convention in late 2023. \n\n Status: Ethnic resistance coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Kuki-Chin languages, Burmese and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Joint military command; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 31 October 2021; Disestablished: 1 December 2023; Succeeded by: Chinland Council; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Republic of Türkiye
description: The Republic of Türkiye is a transcontinental sovereign republic situated across the Anatolian Peninsula in West Asia and East Thrace in South-Eastern Europe. On 31 May 2022, the United Nations formally registered the country's change of international denomination from Turkey to Türkiye, reflecting an official campaign to preserve national cultural prestige and historic linguistic heritage. Administered from its political capital at Ankara, the state commands a major economic and strategic presence spanning the Mediterranean and Black Sea basins while playing an influential role in Middle Eastern, Caucasian and European geopolitical affairs. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Ankara; Largest city: Istanbul; Official languages: Turkish; Religion: Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Grand National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 31 May 2022; Preceded by: Republic of Turkey; Currency: Turkish lira

name: Karenni Army
description: The Karenni Army served as the primary armed wing of the Karenni National Progressive Party, defending the ethnic Karenni population in eastern Myanmar's rugged Kayah State. Stationed administratively in the southern border township of Hpasawng, the force spearheaded widespread armed resistance against the central military junta during the intensification of the nationwide civil war. Working in close cooperation with newly created local defence militias, the army conducted coordinated operations that effectively neutralised junta troop mobility across key river valleys, maintaining territorial self-governance until broader regional administration was consolidated under the Karenni State Interim Executive Council. \n\n Status: Ethnic revolutionary armed force; Administrative seat: Hpasawng; Common languages: Karenni and Burmese; Religion: Christianity, Buddhism and Animism; Government: Military high command; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 September 2022; Disestablished: 12 June 2023; Succeeded by: Karenni State Interim Executive Council; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Coalition of Patriots for Change
description: The Coalition of Patriots for Change is an armed rebel alliance in the Central African Republic formed by uniting major ex-Séléka factions and Anti-balaka militia commands under the leadership of former president François Bozizé. Operating without a conventional civil capital, the insurgent umbrella was established to disrupt national elections and overthrow the government in Bangui. Functioning through decentralised regional sectors across the northern and western prefectures, the coalition maintains persistent bush warfare, mounting asymmetric strikes against national army garrisons and foreign security contractors while collecting informal tolls along international transit corridors. \n\n Status: Insurgent rebel coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Sango and French; Religion: Christianity, Animism and Islam; Government: Rebel military supreme council; Head of state: François Bozizé; Historical era: Central African Republic Civil War; Established: 9 September 2022; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Sool, Sanaag, and Cayn-Khatumo Administration
description: The Sool, Sanaag, and Cayn-Khatumo Administration was established on 6 February 2023 as an autonomous regional governing authority by Dhulbahante clan elders and local leaders in northern Somalia. Operating from its capital at Las Anod, the administration was proclaimed following intense civil unrest and prolonged urban combat that successfully expelled the armed forces of the self-declared Republic of Somaliland. Rejecting Somaliland's territorial claims in favour of direct union with the Federal Government of Somalia, the interim leadership administered the contested eastern borderlands until securing official recognition from Mogadishu as a federal member administration in October 2023. \n\n Status: Autonomous regional administration; Capital and largest city: Las Anod; Official languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional clan council; Historical era: Somali civil war; Established: 6 February 2023; Disestablished: 19 October 2023; Succeeded by: North Eastern State of Somalia; Currency: Somali shilling

name: Rapid Support Forces
description: The Rapid Support Forces is a powerful Sudanese paramilitary organisation commanded by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo that erupted into open warfare against the Sudanese Armed Forces in April 2023. Originating from the Janjaweed auxiliary militias of Darfur, the faction mounted a coordinated blitz to capture military bases and public ministries throughout the capital city of Khartoum. Dominating vast swathes of western and central Sudan, the force established parallel military administrations across occupied territories while engaging in protracted warfare that displaced millions and devastated national infrastructure. \n\n Status: Insurgent paramilitary army; Administrative seat: Khartoum; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military supreme command; Head of state: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo; Historical era: Sudanese civil war; Established: 15 April 2023; Currency: Sudanese pound

name: Karenni State Interim Executive Council
description: The Karenni State Interim Executive Council is a provisional revolutionary government established on 12 June 2023 to coordinate administrative, judicial and civil functions across liberated territories in eastern Myanmar's Karenni State. Headquartered in Demoso, the council was formed through a consensus between the Karenni National Progressive Party, local People's Defence Forces and civil society representatives. Functioning as a transitional state administration independent of the central military junta, the executive manages public health clinics, primary education, revenue collection and local security while actively laying the constitutional foundations for a future democratic federal union. \n\n Status: Provisional revolutionary government; Capital: Demoso; Common languages: Karenni and Burmese; Religion: Christianity, Buddhism and Animism; Government: Transitional executive council; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 12 June 2023; Preceded by: Karenni Army; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North
description: The Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North is an armed political organisation advocating for secularism, ethnic equality and local autonomy across the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan and the Blue Nile region in Sudan. Led by Abdelaziz al-Hilu, the movement administers an extensive liberated territory termed New Sudan from its secluded mountain stronghold at Kauda. Following the outbreak of the Sudanese civil war between federal armed forces and the Rapid Support Forces in 2023, the movement's military wing launched targeted offensives to expand its security perimeter, maintaining stable civil institutions, courts and schools despite nationwide instability. \n\n Status: De facto autonomous administration; Capital: Kauda; Common languages: Nuba languages, Arabic and English; Religion: Christianity, Islam and traditional beliefs; Government: Revolutionary command council; Head of state: Abdelaziz al-Hilu; Historical era: Sudanese civil war; Established: 21 June 2023; Currency: Sudanese pound

name: Wagner Private Military Company
description: The Wagner Private Military Company staged a brief armed mutiny within the Russian Federation between 23 and 25 June 2023 under the direction of its oligarch leader Yevgeny Prigozhin. Having played a central frontline combat role during the invasion of Ukraine, the paramilitary force revolted against the leadership of the Russian Ministry of Defence, rapidly seizing the Southern Military District headquarters in Rostov-on-Don without encountering resistance. Establishing Rostov-on-Don as an impromptu operational capital, heavily armed Wagner columns advanced northwards towards Moscow before Prigozhin accepted a Belarusian-mediated deal, halting the rebellion and dispersing the mercenary cadre. \n\n Status: Mutinous private military corporation; Administrative seat: Rostov-on-Don; Official languages: Russian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Mercenary military leadership; Head of state: Yevgeny Prigozhin; Historical era: Russo-Ukrainian war; Established: 23 June 2023; Disestablished: 25 June 2023; Currency: Russian ruble

name: Sudan Liberation Movement/Army
description: The Sudan Liberation Movement/Army represents a formidable secular rebel movement active throughout the mountainous Jebel Marra region of Darfur in western Sudan. Led by historic founder Abdul Wahid al-Nur, the faction resisted successive peace accords with Khartoum, insisting on comprehensive democratic restructuring and international protection for indigenous Fur, Zaghawa and Masalit communities. Administered from its redoubt at Tur, the movement preserved a de facto autonomous enclave, providing essential local governance and civilian sanctuary as surrounding Darfuri cities succumbed to brutal warfare between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. \n\n Status: Autonomous insurgent administration; Administrative seat: Tur; Common languages: Fur, Arabic and English; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Revolutionary military council; Head of state: Abdul Wahid al-Nur; Historical era: War in Darfur and Sudanese civil war; Established: 23 September 2023; Currency: Sudanese pound

name: Chin Brotherhood Alliance
description: The Chin Brotherhood Alliance is an armed coalition of regional Chin defence forces formed in western Myanmar to coordinate military operations and civilian administration across Chin State. Established by township resistance groups that rejected the centralised Chinland Constitution as insufficiently democratic and unrepresentative of local communities, the alliance encompasses fighters from Mindat, Matupi, Kanpetlet and surrounding areas. Operating without a singular capital through consultative field councils, the coalition collaborated closely with the Arakan Army to liberate towns from junta occupation, eventually moving towards unifying its constituent brigades into a consolidated Chin People's Army in early 2026. \n\n Status: Regional ethnic military alliance; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Kuki-Chin languages and Burmese; Religion: Christianity; Government: Joint revolutionary council; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 December 2023; Historical region: Chin State; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Chinland Council
description: The Chinland Council briefly operated as the constitutional convention and transitional authority responsible for drafting the fundamental governing charter of the Chin people in western Myanmar. Meeting at the Chin National Front headquarters at Camp Victoria, the constituent assembly brought together over two hundred representatives, including elected parliamentarians from the 2020 elections, revolutionary commanders and local tribal leaders. Chaired by Pu Zing Cung, the council established the political blueprint and administrative apparatus for self-determination, concluding its transitional convening on 6 December 2023 with the formal ratification of the Chinland Constitution and the proclamation of the State of Chinland. \n\n Status: Constituent assembly and transitional council; Capital: Camp Victoria; Official languages: Burmese, Kuki-Chin languages and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Transitional constituent assembly; Head of state: Pu Zing Cung; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 December 2023; Disestablished: 6 December 2023; Succeeded by: State of Chinland

name: State of Chinland
description: The State of Chinland is an autonomous self-governing ethnic polity established across western Myanmar following the formal adoption of the Chinland Constitution in December 2023. Governed by the Chinland Council from its administrative headquarters at Camp Victoria, the state exercises de facto sovereignty over approximately one third of Chin State along the borders with India and Bangladesh. Defended primarily by the Chin National Army and allied local defence units, the administration oversees regional courts, emergency public health, education and customs collection, functioning as a constituent member of the broader federal democratic movement against the Naypyidaw junta. \n\n Status: Autonomous self-governing ethnic state; Capital: Camp Victoria; Official languages: Burmese, Kuki-Chin languages and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Semi-presidential federal state; Legislature: Chinland Council; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 6 December 2023; Preceded by: Chinland Council; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Karen National Army
description: The Karen National Army is an ethnic armed organisation active across south-eastern Myanmar's Kayin State, established when the Karen Border Guard Force declared its independence from the ruling military junta in early 2024. Descended from the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army and led by Colonel Saw Chit Thu, the force maintains its administrative base at the border enclave of Shwe Kokko. By severing ties with the central army, the force asserted autonomous territorial control over lucrative trade corridors, casino developments and commercial zones along the Moei River bordering Thailand. \n\n Status: Autonomous ethnic border force; Administrative seat: Shwe Kokko; Common languages: Karen, Burmese and Thai; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Military administrative command; Head of state: Saw Chit Thu; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2024; Currency: Myanmar kyat and Thai baht

name: New Mon State Party
description: The New Mon State Party is a veteran ethnic political organisation representing the Mon population of southern Myanmar that experienced internal divergence in early 2024 amid the intensifying civil war. Headquartered administratively in Ye Township within Mon State, the party's military wing, the Mon National Liberation Army, split into an anti-junta faction committed to armed revolution alongside pro-democracy forces and a conservative leadership faction maintaining formal ceasefire dialogues. Exercising territorial control over isolated rural pockets, the movement provides local administration, judicial arbitrations and Mon-language schooling while navigating shifting political alignments across the Tenasserim coastline. \n\n Status: Ethnic political party and armed administration; Administrative seat: Ye; Common languages: Mon and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Revolutionary party executive; Head of state: Nai Hong Sar; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 1 February 2024; Historical region: Mon State; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Arakha Army
description: The Arakha Army is the reconstituted designation of the Arakan Army, representing all residents of Rakhine State regardless of ethnic or religious heritage in western Myanmar. Administered from the historic inland capital of Mrauk-U by Commander-in-Chief Twan Mrat Naing, the military force adopted this inclusive title in April 2024 to reflect its transition from an ethnic insurgent militia into a comprehensive sovereign state administration. Having seized almost all major townships and military garrisons across northern Rakhine, the army manages maritime seaports, public hospitals, policing and legal tribunals while consolidating its borders against remnants of the retreating junta. \n\n Status: De facto sovereign state administration; Capital: Mrauk-U; Official languages: Rakhine and Burmese; Common languages: Rakhine, Burmese and Rohingya; Religion: Theravada Buddhism and Islam; Government: Revolutionary military administration; Ruler title: Commander-in-Chief; First ruler: Twan Mrat Naing; Historical era: Myanmar civil war; Established: 10 April 2024; Preceded by: Arakan Army; Currency: Myanmar kyat

name: Zomi Revolutionary Army
description: The Zomi Revolutionary Army is an ethnic insurgent paramilitary organisation operating across the porous frontier separating north-eastern India's state of Manipur from the Chin Hills of Myanmar. Established as the military wing of the Zomi Re-unification Organisation and based in the market town of Churachandpur, the group was formed to protect the Zomi and Paite communities amidst fierce inter-ethnic strife. In mid-2024, the army expanded its active cross-border presence, enforcing local security cordons and village self-defence patrols while navigating intense ethnic friction in Manipur and coordinating tactical rear-bases within adjoining Myanmar borderlands. \n\n Status: Armed ethnic insurgent organisation; Administrative seat: Churachandpur; Common languages: Zomi, Paite and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Revolutionary military council; Head of state: Thanglianpau Guite; Historical era: Contemporary border conflicts; Established: 16 May 2024; Currency: Indian rupee and Myanmar kyat

name: Ukraine (Military Occupation)
description: Ukraine established an unexpected military occupation across the Kursk Oblast of the Russian Federation following a surprise cross-border incursion launched on 6 August 2024. Establishing its forward command and administrative commandant's office in the seized town of Sudzha, the Ukrainian military assumed operational control over dozens of settlements and key natural gas metering infrastructure. Administered by appointed military commanders without civilian annexations, this occupation zone provided a strategic buffer against Russian cross-border shelling, facilitated prisoner exchanges and served as a crucial bargaining instrument in the broader Russo-Ukrainian War. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: Sudzha; Official languages: Ukrainian and Russian; Government: Military administrative command; Historical era: Russo-Ukrainian war; Established: 6 August 2024; Preceded by: Russian Federation; Currency: Ukrainian hryvnia and Russian ruble

name: Military Operations Command
description: The Military Operations Command was a unified rebel operations room established by northern Syrian opposition factions that spearheaded the decisive late-2024 offensive against the Baathist regime of Bashar al-Assad. Evolving from the Idlib-based Al-Fatah al-Mubin coalition, the command coordinated Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham, the Turkish-backed National Front for Liberation and Jaysh al-Izza. Launching a lightning assault from Idlib, the allied command captured Syria's second city of Aleppo in late November 2024 and established it as their operational command centre, rapidly collapsing governmental defensive lines across Hama and Homs before dissolving upon the formation of the national transitional administration. \n\n Status: Joint military command council; Capital: Aleppo; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unified military operations council; Historical era: Syrian civil war; Established: 27 November 2024; Disestablished: 10 December 2024; Preceded by: Syrian Arab Republic (Ba'athist); Succeeded by: Syrian Arab Republic (Transitional Government)

name: Southern Operations Room
description: The Southern Operations Room was an armed Syrian opposition coalition established on 6 December 2024 to direct anti-Assad forces across the southern governorates of Daraa, Suwayda and Quneitra. Centred in the southern provincial capital of Daraa, the command brought together dozens of local brigades in operational coordination with northern advances. Sweeping through regional garrisons, the coalition entered the capital city of Damascus during the collapse of the Baathist government, before ceding municipal authority to the newly established national transitional administration and preparing to integrate into the central Ministry of Defence. \n\n Status: Joint military command council; Capital: Daraa; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unified military operational room; Historical era: Syrian civil war; Established: 6 December 2024; Disestablished: 10 December 2024; Preceded by: Syrian Arab Republic (Ba'athist); Succeeded by: Syrian Arab Republic (Transitional Government)

name: Syrian Arab Republic
description: The Syrian Arab Republic entered a transformative transitional phase on 10 December 2024 following the capture of Damascus and the collapse of the fifty-four-year Baathist regime. Operating under the provisional authority of Ahmed al-Sharaa and Prime Minister Mohammed al-Bashir, the new government established its seat in the historic capital of Damascus to lead national stabilisation. The administration initiated sweeping institutional reorganisations, dissolving disparate rebel paramilitary factions into a regular army, restoring basic civil infrastructure and enacting a constitutional declaration to preserve state integrity while laying the groundwork for inclusive parliamentary democracy. \n\n Status: Sovereign state under provisional government; Capital and largest city: Damascus; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic under a provisional government; Head of state: Ahmed al-Sharaa; Historical era: Post-Assad transition; Established: 10 December 2024; Preceded by: Syrian Arab Republic (Ba'athist); Currency: Syrian pound
